doc: The canonical description of mcpd's data model and HTTP surface. Every SDK type, every generated docs page and the OpenAPI document are produced from this file. Nothing downstream is hand-written.

SpanKind.doc: What an operation *is*. The kind drives how a span is rendered in the waterfall, which attributes are meaningful, and which metrics are auto-extracted from it.

values.name: agent_run
values.doc: One agent invocation. Usually the root of a trace.

values.name: model_generation
values.doc: One logical generation: everything from the first request to the final answer, including every intermediate step.

values.name: model_step
values.doc: One step inside a generation. A generation that calls tools twice has three steps.

values.name: model_inference
values.doc: The provider round-trip alone, excluding processors and tool execution. Measure pure model latency here.

values.name: model_chunk
values.doc: A single streamed chunk. Recorded as an event, not a duration.

values.name: tool_call
values.doc: A tool your code executes.

values.name: client_tool_call
values.doc: A tool the calling client executes. The server records the marker; the client returns the detail.

values.name: provider_tool_call
values.doc: A tool the model provider executes server-side, such as hosted web search or code execution.

values.name: mcp_tool_call
values.doc: A tool reached over the Model Context Protocol.

values.name: workflow_run
values.doc: One workflow execution. Usually the root of a trace.

values.name: workflow_step
values.doc: One step within a workflow.

values.name: workflow_conditional
values.doc: A branch point, with the conditions it evaluated.

values.name: workflow_conditional_eval
values.doc: One condition evaluated inside a branch point.

values.name: workflow_parallel
values.doc: A fan-out of concurrent branches.

values.name: workflow_loop
values.doc: A loop construct: foreach, do-while or do-until.

values.name: workflow_sleep
values.doc: A deliberate pause.

values.name: workflow_wait_event
values.doc: A wait for an external event, with its timeout.

values.name: memory_operation
values.doc: A read from or write to agent memory.

values.name: rag_ingestion
values.doc: One ingestion pipeline run: load, chunk, extract, embed, upsert.

values.name: rag_embedding
values.doc: One embedding call, possibly batched.

values.name: rag_vector_operation
values.doc: Vector store I/O: query, upsert, delete or fetch.

values.name: rag_action
values.doc: A RAG-specific transform: chunk, extract metadata or rerank.

values.name: graph_action
values.doc: A graph build, traverse, update or prune.

values.name: processor_run
values.doc: An input or output processor.

values.name: scorer_run
values.doc: One scorer evaluating a target.

values.name: scorer_step
values.doc: One stage of a scorer's pipeline.

values.name: guardrail
values.doc: A safety or policy check, and whether it tripped.

values.name: retrieval
values.doc: A generic retrieval that is not vector-store specific.

values.name: mapping
values.doc: An inline data transform between pipeline stages.

values.name: skill_resolution
values.doc: A dynamic resolver deciding which skills an agent may use.

values.name: workspace_action
values.doc: A filesystem, sandbox, search or computer-use action.

values.name: http_request
values.doc: An outbound HTTP call made on the agent's behalf.

values.name: generic
values.doc: Anything else. Always valid; never inferred.

values.name: unset
values.doc: Still running, or the producer never said.

values.name: ok
values.doc: Completed successfully.

values.name: error
values.doc: Failed. `error` carries the detail.

values.name: cancelled
values.doc: Abandoned deliberately, by a caller or a timeout.

SignalType.doc: The six signals mcpd stores. Every one of them is correlated by trace id, most of them by span id as well, and every one of them passes through the same redaction pipeline.

values.name: span
values.doc: A unit of work with a start and, usually, an end.

values.name: log
values.doc: A structured log record.

values.name: metric
values.doc: A numeric observation.

values.name: score
values.doc: A machine evaluation of a span or trace.

values.name: feedback
values.doc: A human evaluation of a span or trace.

values.name: aspect_note
values.doc: One sentence recorded against a trace along one aspect. Stored, redacted and retained like the other five, and erased with the subject it belongs to.

values.name: trace
values.doc: Finer than debug. Off by default.

values.name: debug
values.doc: Detail useful while diagnosing.

values.name: info
values.doc: Normal operation.

values.name: warn
values.doc: Recoverable, but worth reading.

values.name: error
values.doc: The operation failed.

values.name: fatal
values.doc: The process cannot continue.

values.name: counter
values.doc: Monotonically increasing. Aggregates by sum.

values.name: gauge
values.doc: A point-in-time value. Aggregates by last, min, max or mean.

values.name: histogram
values.doc: A distribution. Aggregates by bucket, and answers quantiles.

SamplingKind.doc: How mcpd decides which traces to keep.

values.name: always
values.doc: Keep everything. The default, and correct until volume says otherwise.

values.name: never
values.doc: Keep nothing. Useful to disable a single project without redeploying.

values.name: ratio
values.doc: Keep a fixed fraction, decided once at the root so a trace is never half-recorded.

values.name: deterministic
values.doc: Keep a fixed fraction, decided by hashing the trace id. Every collector in a fleet makes the same decision without coordinating.

values.name: tail
values.doc: Buffer the trace, then decide once it finishes. Keeps every error and every slow trace regardless of rate.

RedactionMode.doc: What happens to a value a redaction rule matched.

values.name: drop
values.doc: Remove the key entirely, as if it was never sent.

values.name: mask
values.doc: Replace the whole value with a fixed token.

values.name: partial
values.doc: Keep a documented prefix and suffix, mask the middle. Enough to recognise a value without disclosing it.

values.name: hash
values.doc: Replace with a keyed SHA-256 digest. Equal inputs stay equal, so you can still group and join, but the original cannot be recovered.

ScoreSource.doc: Where a score came from. Kept separate from the scorer's identity so the same scorer can run in more than one context.

values.name: live
values.doc: Produced online, as the traced run happened.

values.name: offline
values.doc: Produced later, by scoring stored traces.

values.name: experiment
values.doc: Produced by an experiment run against a dataset.

values.name: manual
values.doc: Entered by a person, through the API or the UI.

FeedbackKind.doc: The shape of a human judgement.

values.name: thumbs
values.doc: Binary. `value` is `up` or `down`.

values.name: rating
values.doc: Ordinal. `value` is a number inside the scale the producer declares.

values.name: correction
values.doc: The right answer. `value` is text.

values.name: tag
values.doc: A label chosen from a set. `value` is the label.

values.name: comment
values.doc: Free prose, with no score attached.

EntityKind.doc: The named thing a span belongs to. Bounded and low-cardinality, so it is safe as a metric label.

values.name: agent
values.doc: An agent.

values.name: workflow
values.doc: A workflow.

values.name: tool
values.doc: A tool.

values.name: model
values.doc: A model.

values.name: scorer
values.doc: A scorer.

values.name: processor
values.doc: A processor.

values.name: pipeline
values.doc: A RAG or data pipeline.

values.name: service
values.doc: A plain service with no richer identity.

ExperimentStatus.doc: Where an experiment run has got to.

values.name: pending
values.doc: Created, not started.

values.name: running
values.doc: In progress.

values.name: succeeded
values.doc: Every item completed.

values.name: failed
values.doc: Aborted. `error` says why.

values.name: cancelled
values.doc: Stopped by a person.

AuditResult.doc: Whether authorisation let the request through.

values.name: allowed
values.doc: The key carried the scope the endpoint needs, so mcpd went on to handle the request.

values.name: refused
values.doc: Authorisation refused the request before it reached storage. Recording the attempt is the point of the row.

RunStatus.doc: Where a run is. Only `running` can move; the other four are terminal, and a terminal run holds no deadline, no wait and no live attempt.

values.name: running
values.doc: Making progress, or waiting for something that will move it: a lease, a timer or an event.

values.name: succeeded
values.doc: Reached the end of the graph. `output` holds what the definition's `output` template rendered, when it declares one.

values.name: failed
values.doc: Ended on an error nothing handled: a step that failed under `on_error: fail_run`, a spent ceiling, or a cancelled child. `error` says which.

values.name: timed_out
values.doc: Ended because the run's own deadline passed.

values.name: cancelled
values.doc: Ended because a caller asked, through the cancel endpoint or by cancelling an ancestor run.

AttemptStatus.doc: Where one attempt at one step is. Four states are live and four are terminal, and the daemon never shows a live attempt on an ended run.

values.name: pending
values.doc: On disk and offerable to a worker, once its retry timer, if any, has fired.

values.name: leased
values.doc: Held by a worker that has not yet posted `started`.

values.name: started
values.doc: Held by a worker that has posted `started`, so a body is running.

values.name: orphaned
values.doc: The lease expired with no heartbeat. Not offerable while the reclaim window is open: a heartbeat inside the window restores the attempt, and a window that closes with no contact requeues it or fails the run, depending on `effect` and on whether the body had started.

values.name: succeeded
values.doc: Finished with an output.

values.name: failed
values.doc: Finished with an error, or marked failed because the run ended while the attempt was live.

values.name: timed_out
values.doc: The step's own deadline passed before the attempt ended.

values.name: skipped
values.doc: Never ran, because the step's `when` guard was false.

StepKind.doc: What a step attempt is an attempt at. `task` and `agent` are claimable. A `wait` row is written by the event that resumes it or the deadline that ends it, so a wait's output and status read like any other step's.

values.name: task
values.doc: Claimable work. The worker runs whatever code it registered under this step id.

values.name: agent
values.doc: Claimable work whose body is the worker's own agent loop. Identical on the wire to `task`; the kind is recorded so the trace and the interface can tell an agent turn from a plain step.

values.name: wait
values.doc: A suspension the daemon resumes on an event or ends on a deadline. Never offered to a worker.

ConstructKind.doc: What a run's cursor names: the construct at its current position in the definition's `steps`. Every kind except `end` is a node kind a definition can declare.

values.name: task
values.doc: Claimable work.

values.name: agent
values.doc: Claimable work whose body is the worker's agent loop.

values.name: sleep
values.doc: A relative delay, in milliseconds. No process is alive during it.

values.name: sleep_until
values.doc: An absolute delay, to an RFC 3339 instant rendered from a template.

values.name: wait_event
values.doc: A suspension addressed by an event name and a key rendered per run.

values.name: parallel
values.doc: A fixed fan-out over named branches, each branch one claimable step. Done when every branch has ended.

values.name: foreach
values.doc: A fan-out over the items of an array, each item one claimable step, with at most `concurrency` of them offerable at once.

values.name: loop
values.doc: A bounded loop whose body is one claimable step per iteration, ended by `until` or by `max_iterations`.

values.name: subworkflow
values.doc: A child run of another definition. Its output becomes this step's output, and a cancel walks down into it.

values.name: end
values.doc: The end of the graph. Never declared in a definition: the cursor reaches it when the last step has ended.

Effect.doc: What running a step body twice would cost, which is what the daemon branches on when a lease is lost. Default `at_least_once`.

values.name: at_least_once
values.doc: Running the body twice is acceptable. A lost lease requeues the attempt. The default.

values.name: at_most_once
values.doc: Running the body twice is not acceptable. `started` must be posted before the body runs, and a started attempt whose lease is lost fails the run rather than running again.

TimerKind.doc: Every deadline the daemon keeps. Each one is a row the tick fires, and each firing is a transaction that moves the run.

values.name: sleep
values.doc: A `sleep` or `sleep_until` coming due.

values.name: lease_expiry
values.doc: A lease that has not been heartbeated. Firing moves the attempt to `orphaned` and opens a reclaim window one lease length long.

values.name: reclaim
values.doc: The close of the reclaim window an expired lease opened. Firing requeues the attempt or fails the run, depending on `effect` and on whether the body had started.

values.name: run_timeout
values.doc: The whole run's ceiling, from `limits.run_timeout_ms`.

values.name: step_timeout
values.doc: One attempt's ceiling, from the node's `step_timeout_ms`. It bounds a worker that heartbeats for ever.

values.name: wait_timeout
values.doc: A `wait_event` whose event has not arrived by `timeout_ms`.

values.name: retry
values.doc: The backoff before a requeued attempt becomes claimable. Firing writes the next attempt as `pending`.

RunEventKind.doc: What a row in a run's event log records. Every row is written in the transaction that made the change it describes, so a reader that has seen sequence number n has seen every change below it.

values.name: run_started
values.doc: The run was created. Payload: `definition_id`, `definition_version`.

values.name: run_cursor
values.doc: The cursor moved. Payload: `index`, `construct`, and `step_key` when the construct has one.

values.name: step_leased
values.doc: A worker claimed an attempt. Payload: `step_key`, `attempt`, `worker_id`.

values.name: step_started
values.doc: A worker posted `started`. Payload: `step_key`, `attempt`.

values.name: step_finished
values.doc: An attempt succeeded. Payload: `step_key`, `attempt`.

values.name: step_failed
values.doc: An attempt failed. Payload: `step_key`, `attempt`, `class`, `message`, `attempts_left`.

values.name: step_skipped
values.doc: A `when` guard was false. Payload: `step_key`.

values.name: run_waiting
values.doc: The run reached a `wait_event`. Payload: `step_key`, `event`, `key`, `expires_at`.

values.name: run_resumed
values.doc: An event resumed a waiting run. Payload: `step_key`, `event_id`.

values.name: run_ended
values.doc: The run reached a terminal status. Payload: `status`, and `error` when there is one.

DefinitionKind.doc: What kind of thing a definition describes.

values.name: workflow
values.doc: A graph of steps the daemon walks. The only kind in version 1: `agent` definitions arrive with the in-process agent loop, which is not served yet.

EventOutcome.doc: What the daemon did with a published event.

values.name: delivered
values.doc: A waiting run took it and moved, in the same transaction.

values.name: parked
values.doc: No run was waiting. The event is held for 24 hours for the next run that reaches a matching wait with `accept_parked`.

values.name: duplicate
values.doc: This event id has been seen before, so nothing was written. The publish endpoint says when a derived id is treated this way.

ConflictReason.doc: Why a worker call about a lease answered 409. Each reason tells the worker something different to do next.

values.name: fenced
values.doc: A later attempt exists, or another lease terminated this attempt. Abandon the work and post nothing more for this lease.

values.name: already_applied
values.doc: This lease's own earlier `complete` or `fail` landed and its reply was lost. The step is done; `attempt_status` says how. Post nothing more.

values.name: not_started
values.doc: `complete` or `fail` arrived for a `leased` attempt under `at_most_once`. A bug in the worker: post `started` first, and log it loudly.

values.name: run_terminal
values.doc: The run has ended. Stop, and stop claiming for this run.

StepErrorClass.doc: How a step failed, which decides whether the daemon retries it.

values.name: retryable
values.doc: Worth another attempt. The daemon retries while attempts remain, at the node's backoff, and honours `retry_after_ms` when it is larger.

values.name: fatal
values.doc: Another attempt would fail the same way. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.

values.name: invalid_input
values.doc: The step's input cannot be acted on. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.

values.name: unservable
values.doc: This worker does not serve the definition version, or does not recognise the step key. The attempt returns to `pending` after one lease length without spending the retry budget, so another worker can take it.

values.name: cancelled
values.doc: The worker gave the attempt up on request. No retry; the node's `on_error` applies.

OnError.doc: What happens to a run when a node fails after its retries. Default `fail_run`.

values.name: fail_run
values.doc: End the run `failed`, with the step's error message as the run's error.

values.name: continue
values.doc: Mark the step `failed` and move on, so a later `when` guard can read `steps.<id>.status` and `steps.<id>.error`.

Backoff.doc: How the delay between retries grows.

values.name: fixed
values.doc: Every retry waits `initial_ms`.

values.name: exponential
values.doc: Each retry waits twice as long as the last, starting at `initial_ms` and capped at `max_ms`.

WaitTimeout.doc: What a `wait_event` node does when its deadline passes with no event. Default `fail`.

values.name: fail
values.doc: The node fails. Its `on_error` decides what the run does next.

values.name: continue
values.doc: The wait ends and the run moves on to the next node.

ValueKind.doc: The JSON type of a value. Used where mcpd reports the shape of something it holds without returning the thing itself.

values.name: null
values.doc: The value was JSON null.

values.name: boolean
values.doc: The value was `true` or `false`.

values.name: number
values.doc: The value was a JSON number.

values.name: string
values.doc: The value was a JSON string.

values.name: array
values.doc: The value was a JSON array.

values.name: object
values.doc: The value was a JSON object.

MonitorWatch.doc: What a monitor measures over its window.

values.name: error_rate
values.doc: The fraction of runs that failed, 0 to 1.

values.name: latency_p95
values.doc: Run duration at the ninety-fifth percentile, in milliseconds.

values.name: cost
values.doc: Total spend across the window.

values.name: trace_count
values.doc: How many runs happened. Catches a pipeline that has gone silent.

values.name: score_mean
values.doc: The mean of the scorer named by `scorer_id`.

values.name: step_count_divergence
values.doc: How far a run strays from the usual shape of its own definition. This watch sets no threshold in steps, because a step count is never high in absolute terms, only high for that definition. It reads the recent completed runs of one definition version, takes the median step count as the usual shape, and reports a run whose modified z-score against the median absolute deviation exceeds the monitor's bound, 3.5 by default. The median absolute deviation is used rather than a mean and a standard deviation because it tolerates up to half its sample being outliers, which is the case here: a runaway cohort must not be allowed to redefine normal. Fewer than twelve completed runs and the watch says nothing rather than guessing. A run that takes several times its usual number of steps trips this long before it reaches `max_steps`, and while its error rate is still zero.

values.name: run_repetition
values.doc: How much a run repeats itself. For each run in the window, the highest number of attempts it made at any one node of its definition, counting a retry and a loop iteration of that node alike; the watch reads the mean of that number. One means no node ran twice. A loop that re-enters the same node, and a retry storm, both raise this before either reaches `error_rate`.

MonitorCompare.doc: Which way a monitor's threshold is breached.

values.name: above
values.doc: Trip when the value rises above the threshold.

values.name: below
values.doc: Trip when the value falls below it. This is the direction that catches a quality regression, and a silent pipeline.

MonitorCondition.doc: Where a monitor or an objective stands. A tripped condition latches: it stays tripped until the number recovers, and too little data never clears it, because silence is not recovery.

values.name: nominal
values.doc: Evaluated, and within its threshold.

values.name: tripped
values.doc: Tripped, and not yet acknowledged.

values.name: acknowledged
values.doc: Tripped, acknowledged, and still breaching. Returns to `nominal` on its own when the number recovers.

values.name: insufficient
values.doc: Not enough data in the window to judge. Also the state before the first evaluation.

TextSearch.doc: What the `q` parameter matches on this deployment's storage backend. Reported by `GET /v1/api/capabilities` so a search box can say what it searches instead of leaving a reader to infer it from a result set.

values.name: none
values.doc: `q` is not applied at all. No backend that ships declares this; a backend that did would be telling an interface to hide its search box rather than let somebody type into one that returns everything.

values.name: substring
values.doc: `q` matches anywhere inside a word, so `heck` finds `checkout`.

values.name: words
values.doc: `q` matches whole words only, which is what a person typing two words into a search box expects. There is no stemming: `refund` does not find `refunds`.

Partitioning.doc: How the storage backend cuts each signal table on its anchor time. It decides whether expiring a day of data is a metadata operation on one part or a row-by-row delete.

values.name: none
values.doc: One table, no partitions. Retention removes rows.

values.name: day
values.doc: One partition per day.

values.name: month
values.doc: One partition per month.

Facet.doc: A dimension a filter box can offer values for. The set is closed on purpose: each one is a column or a parsed field the daemon keeps a distinct-value list for as signals arrive, so answering is a read of a small table rather than a scan of every span in the retention window.

values.name: entity_kind
values.doc: The kind of thing a step was: an agent run, a tool call, a retrieval, and so on.

values.name: entity_name
values.doc: The name of that thing, such as the tool that was called.

values.name: service_name
values.doc: The service that reported the signal.

values.name: environment
values.doc: The environment it came from, such as `production`.

values.name: tag
values.doc: A tag carried on a run.

values.name: metric_name
values.doc: A metric name, for the name box of a chart.

values.name: metric_label_key
values.doc: A label key a metric point carries. Project-wide: these are every key seen in the project, not the keys of one named metric.

values.name: metric_label_value
values.doc: A value one label key takes. Needs `key`, because the answer would otherwise be every value of every label mixed together.

DeltaSignal.doc: A signal that can be polled for what has arrived. Only the three that carry a server-set arrival time: a score and a piece of feedback are stamped with the caller's own timestamp, so a watermark over them would either skip a late row or repeat every row for ever.

values.name: traces
values.doc: The run projection, which is what a run list refreshes from.

values.name: spans
values.doc: Steps, for a waterfall that is still filling in.

values.name: logs
values.doc: Log lines.

AspectReadiness.doc: How far the daemon has got with one aspect for one entity. It is computed from the rows that are stored and never recorded, so it cannot go stale, and it is per entity and per aspect rather than global: one agent can have goal themes to read while its behaviour notes are still collecting.

values.name: collecting
values.doc: Fewer notes than a clustering pass needs. The floor is 50 notes for one aspect on one entity, and below it the daemon writes no snapshot at all rather than sorting a handful of sentences into themes nobody should draw a conclusion from.

values.name: processing
values.doc: Enough notes to cluster, and no snapshot covers this aspect yet. The next pass will write one. Nothing is wrong and nothing needs doing.

values.name: ready
values.doc: A snapshot covers this aspect, so themes exist and every theme route answers.

ThemeState.doc: What happened to a theme between the previous snapshot and this one. The daemon matches themes across consecutive snapshots by their wording, so a theme keeps its id while its wording holds, and this records what that match found. It is computed from the two clusterings alone and never from a trace attribute.

values.name: birth
values.doc: The first snapshot this theme appears in.

values.name: continue
values.doc: Present in the previous snapshot and in this one, matched to the same id. The ordinary state of a theme that is holding together.

values.name: split
values.doc: The previous snapshot held one theme where this one holds several. The history point's `split_from` names the theme it came out of.

values.name: merge
values.doc: Several themes in the previous snapshot are one theme here. The history point's `merged_from` names them.

values.name: resurrection
values.doc: Present in an earlier snapshot, absent from the one immediately before this, and back now under its original id. A theme that comes and goes reads as one theme with gaps rather than as several short-lived ones.

values.name: death
values.doc: The theme was in the previous snapshot and is in none of this one's clusters. Reachable only through a theme's history: a dead theme has no row in the snapshot it died in, so it is never a node in a flow.

ThemeNodeKind.doc: What one node of a theme flow stands for. A stage holds its themes, at most one noise node and at most one overflow node, and the three together account for every trace in the stage, which is what lets the shares add up to one.

values.name: theme
values.doc: One theme. It carries a `theme_id`, so it can be filtered on, opened and followed through its history.

values.name: noise
values.doc: The notes in this stage that joined no theme. Noise is not a failure bucket: it holds rare requests, wording nothing else matched and patterns that have not recurred yet, and a large noise share means varied traffic or too few notes rather than something going wrong. Its notes are read from the examples route with `noise` as the theme id.

values.name: other
values.doc: The themes past `theme_limit_per_stage`, folded into one node so the stage totals still add up. It carries no `theme_id` and cannot be selected, filtered on or opened, because it is a presentation fold and not a group of anything.

SnapshotLandmarkReason.doc: Why one snapshot is in a landmark selection. A timeline draws a couple of dozen points over a range that may hold thousands of passes, so the daemon chooses them and says why, rather than handing back the newest few and leaving the reader to assume that is the whole story.

values.name: range_start
values.doc: The oldest snapshot in the requested range. Always included, so a timeline starts where the range does.

values.name: range_end
values.doc: The newest snapshot in the requested range. Always included, so a timeline ends at the current state.

values.name: time_sample
values.doc: Chosen to spread the remaining points evenly over the range. Sampling is by time and not by ordinal, so an hour of frequent passes does not crowd out a quiet week.

KeyScope.doc: What an account API key may do. The same six scopes the daemon's configured keys carry, under the same names as the `auth` value of each endpoint.

values.name: ingest
values.doc: Write signals, and read nothing. The key that lives in every process that emits a span.

values.name: read
values.doc: Read stored signals: runs, spans, logs, metrics, scores, analytics and datasets.

values.name: write
values.doc: Change stored data: scores, feedback, datasets, experiments and acknowledgements.

values.name: admin
values.doc: Delete data and read the audit log. Also accepted where `execute` or `worker` is needed.

values.name: execute
values.doc: Start, cancel and signal runs, and publish events to them.

values.name: worker
values.doc: Claim steps and report their outcome. The key that lives in the process running step bodies.

OrgRole.doc: What a member may do in an organisation. Each role maps onto the six key scopes on every project the organisation owns, unless a project role says otherwise.

values.name: owner
values.doc: Every scope on every project, and everything an admin may do. Only an owner may add or remove an owner, change quotas or delete the organisation.

values.name: admin
values.doc: Every scope on every project. Invites and removes members below owner, sets roles, creates and deletes projects, and manages SSO, SCIM and every key in the organisation.

values.name: member
values.doc: The `ingest`, `read`, `write`, `execute` and `worker` scopes. Everything but `admin`: a member cannot delete data or read the audit log.

values.name: viewer
values.doc: The `read` scope only.

ProjectRole.doc: A role on one project that replaces a member's organisation role there. Owners and admins keep their reach on every project whatever a project role says.

values.name: none
values.doc: No access to this project.

values.name: viewer
values.doc: The `read` scope on this project.

values.name: member
values.doc: Every scope but `admin` on this project.

values.name: admin
values.doc: Every scope on this project. It does not let the member manage the organisation.

SsoProvider.doc: How an organisation's members log in with single sign-on.

values.name: oidc
values.doc: Any OpenID Connect provider, such as Google, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Auth0, found through its issuer's discovery document. Authorization code flow with PKCE, state and nonce.

values.name: github
values.doc: GitHub, through an OAuth app. GitHub issues no ID token, so the member is the GitHub user id and the email is the primary verified address GitHub reports.

InputTokenDetails.doc: Input tokens broken down by how the provider billed them. Every field is optional; absent means the provider did not report it, which is different from zero.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: Ordinary text tokens: not cached, not audio, not image.

fields.name: cache_read
fields.doc: Tokens served from a prompt cache. Usually billed at a large discount.

fields.name: cache_write
fields.doc: Tokens written into a prompt cache. Usually billed at a premium.

fields.name: cache_write_5m
fields.doc: Tokens written to a five-minute ephemeral cache, where the provider prices TTLs separately.

fields.name: cache_write_1h
fields.doc: Tokens written to a one-hour ephemeral cache.

fields.name: audio
fields.doc: Audio input tokens.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: Image input tokens, including rendered PDF pages.

OutputTokenDetails.doc: Output tokens broken down by kind.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: Ordinary completion tokens.

fields.name: reasoning
fields.doc: Hidden reasoning tokens. Billed, and usually invisible in the response.

fields.name: audio
fields.doc: Audio output tokens.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: Image output tokens.

TokenUsage.doc: Token counts for one model call. Totals are authoritative; the detail breakdowns explain them and are what cost is actually computed from.

fields.name: input_tokens
fields.doc: Total input tokens.

fields.name: output_tokens
fields.doc: Total output tokens.

fields.name: total_tokens
fields.doc: Input plus output, when the provider reports a total that differs from the sum.

fields.name: input_details
fields.doc: How the input tokens were billed.

fields.name: output_details
fields.doc: How the output tokens were billed.

Cost.doc: What a span cost, in a single currency. mcpd computes this from a price book at ingest and stores the result, so a later price change never silently rewrites history.

fields.name: currency
fields.doc: ISO 4217 code. `USD` unless the price book says otherwise.

fields.name: input_cost
fields.doc: Cost attributable to input tokens.

fields.name: output_cost
fields.doc: Cost attributable to output tokens.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.doc: The sum, including any meter that is neither input nor output.

fields.name: price_book
fields.doc: Identifier of the price book used, so a figure can be traced back to the rates that produced it.

fields.name: is_estimated
fields.doc: True when mcpd derived the cost from a price book, false when the producer reported it directly.

ModelParameters.doc: The sampling settings a caller chose for one model call. Recorded because a run nobody can reproduce is a run nobody can debug, and the seed and the sampling settings are what a replay has to match. Every field is what the caller asked for, never what the provider did with it. None of them carries prompt or completion text, so a producer running with payload capture off still records all of them.

fields.name: temperature
fields.doc: The sampling temperature the caller asked for. Absent when the caller left the provider's default in place, which is not the same as sending zero.

fields.name: top_p
fields.doc: Nucleus sampling: the caller asked the sampler to consider the smallest set of tokens whose probabilities reach this fraction. Absent when the caller set none.

fields.name: top_k
fields.doc: The caller asked the sampler to consider only this many of the most likely tokens. Not every provider offers it.

fields.name: max_tokens
fields.doc: The ceiling the caller put on output length. An answer that stops in the middle of a sentence usually stopped here, and this is the first field to read when one does.

fields.name: seed
fields.doc: The sampling seed the caller passed. Nothing in mcpd reads it. It is recorded because without it a run cannot be reproduced at all, and a comparison between two runs that differ only in their seed is worth nothing.

fields.name: stop_sequences
fields.doc: The stop sequences the caller supplied. They are short strings the caller wrote, so they are settings rather than payload, and an answer that ends early often ends on one of them. Do not put prompt text here.

fields.name: has_response_format
fields.doc: True when the caller constrained the output to a fixed shape, such as a JSON schema or a grammar. The shape itself is not recorded: it can be large and it is caller-owned content, and what a reader needs is whether the constraint was on.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: A human-readable message. Required: an error with no message is not actionable.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The error class or code, such as `RateLimitError` or `ECONNRESET`.

fields.name: stack
fields.doc: A stack trace, when the producer captured one.

fields.name: domain
fields.doc: Which subsystem raised it.

fields.name: retryable
fields.doc: Whether the producer considered the failure worth retrying.

fields.name: details
fields.doc: Structured detail. Passes through redaction like any other payload.

Correlation.doc: The descriptive context a signal belongs to. Every field here is queryable and most are safe as metric labels; the high-cardinality ones (`user_id`, `session_id`, `request_id`) are queryable but blocked from metric labels by the cardinality filter.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project this belongs to. The primary tenancy key.

fields.name: environment
fields.doc: Deployment environment, such as `production` or `staging`.

fields.name: service_name
fields.doc: The emitting service.

fields.name: service_version
fields.doc: The emitting service's version, so a regression can be pinned to a release.

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: A user-facing session. Groups many traces into one conversation.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.doc: A conversation thread within a session.

fields.name: user_id
fields.doc: The end user. Hashed with a keyed digest at ingest, so runs can still be grouped by customer without storing who the customer is. Filtering on it hashes your query value the same way, so lookup keeps working. Rotating the key deliberately breaks the link.

fields.name: resource_id
fields.doc: A tenant or workspace inside the calling application.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: The producer's own identifier for this run.

fields.name: request_id
fields.doc: The inbound request that caused this work.

fields.name: experiment_id
fields.doc: Set when the run was produced by an experiment.

fields.name: release
fields.doc: A release or git sha, for regression attribution.

SpanLink.doc: A reference from this span to another, in this trace or a different one. Links express causality that parentage cannot: a batch job caused by twenty requests has twenty links and one parent.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The linked trace.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The linked span, when the link points at one rather than a whole trace.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Why the link exists, such as `follows_from`, `retry_of` or `replay_of`.

fields.name: attributes
fields.doc: Anything else about the relationship.

Page.doc: Cursor pagination. Cursors are opaque and stable; never construct one by hand.

fields.name: next_cursor
fields.doc: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Absent on the last page.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc: Whether another page exists.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Total matching rows, when the backend could count them cheaply.

IngestBatch.doc: One batch of signals sent to the native ingest endpoint. Any combination of the six signals may appear in a single batch; mcpd sorts them out. Supplying `ingest_key` makes the whole batch idempotent, so a client that retries after a timeout never double-counts.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc: Spans to record.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc: Log records to record.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: Metric observations to record.

fields.name: scores
fields.doc: Machine evaluations to attach.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: Human evaluations to attach.

fields.name: aspect_notes
fields.doc: Aspect notes to record. A note is a sentence about a trace, so it arrives with that trace's other signals, under the same idempotency key and through the same redactor.

fields.name: ingest_key
fields.doc: Idempotency key for this batch. Replaying a batch with a key mcpd has already accepted is a no-op that still returns 200.

IngestError.doc: Why one signal in a batch was refused.

fields.name: signal
fields.doc: Which signal kind the failure was in.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: Position within that signal's array, so a client can find the offending record.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What was wrong, in terms the sender can act on.

IngestResult.doc: What mcpd did with a batch. Counts are per signal, and `rejected` is never silently zero: a signal mcpd could not store is always reported with a reason.

fields.name: accepted
fields.doc: How many signals were stored.

fields.name: rejected
fields.doc: How many were refused.

fields.name: duplicate
fields.doc: How many were recognised as a replay of an already-accepted batch and skipped.

fields.name: errors
fields.doc: One entry per rejected signal, naming what was wrong and where.

fields.name: traces
fields.doc: The matching traces, in the requested order.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

TraceDetail.doc: One trace and everything attached to it.

fields.name: trace
fields.doc: The trace projection.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc: Every span, ordered by start time then by depth, so a waterfall renders without sorting.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc: Logs, when `include` asked for them.

fields.name: scores
fields.doc: Scores, when `include` asked for them.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: Feedback, when `include` asked for them.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc: The matching spans.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc: The matching records.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

MetricSeriesPoint.doc: One bucket of an aggregated series.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Start of the bucket.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The aggregated value.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many raw observations fell in this bucket. Distinguishes a genuine zero from no data.

fields.name: exemplar_trace_id
fields.doc: A trace that contributed to this bucket, so a spike on the chart opens the run that caused it.

MetricSeries.doc: One line on a chart: a single label combination over time.

fields.name: labels
fields.doc: The label values that identify this series.

fields.name: points
fields.doc: Bucketed values, oldest first.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The metric queried.

fields.name: unit
fields.doc: UCUM unit, for axis labelling.

fields.name: bucket
fields.doc: The bucket width actually used, which may differ from the request when mcpd chose it.

fields.name: series
fields.doc: One entry per label combination.

fields.name: scores
fields.doc: The matching scores.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: The matching feedback.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

LatencyStats.doc: Latency distribution over a window, in milliseconds.

fields.name: p50
fields.doc: Median.

fields.name: p90
fields.doc: Ninetieth percentile.

fields.name: p95
fields.doc: Ninety-fifth percentile.

fields.name: p99
fields.doc: Ninety-ninth percentile.

fields.name: mean
fields.doc: Arithmetic mean. Reported alongside quantiles, never instead of them.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: Slowest observation in the window.

GroupedStat.doc: One row of a grouped breakdown.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The group's value, such as a model id.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many runs fell in this group.

fields.name: error_count
fields.doc: How many of them failed.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.doc: Spend attributable to this group.

fields.name: input_tokens
fields.doc: Input tokens for this group.

fields.name: output_tokens
fields.doc: Output tokens for this group.

fields.name: latency
fields.doc: Latency distribution within this group.

AnalyticsSummary.doc: Headline numbers for a window. One request backs the overview screen.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Start of the window.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: End of the window.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: Runs started in the window.

fields.name: span_count
fields.doc: Steps recorded in the window.

fields.name: error_count
fields.doc: Runs that failed.

fields.name: error_rate
fields.doc: Failures as a fraction of runs, between 0 and 1.

fields.name: latency
fields.doc: Run duration distribution.

fields.name: input_tokens
fields.doc: Input tokens consumed.

fields.name: output_tokens
fields.doc: Output tokens produced.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.doc: Total spend in the window.

fields.name: currency
fields.doc: Currency of `total_cost`.

fields.name: groups
fields.doc: Per-group rows, when `group_by` was supplied.

CostBucket.doc: Spend in one time bucket for one group.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: Start of the bucket.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The group this row belongs to.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.doc: Spend in this bucket.

fields.name: input_tokens
fields.doc: Input tokens in this bucket.

fields.name: output_tokens
fields.doc: Output tokens in this bucket.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Start of the window.

fields.name: to
fields.doc: End of the window.

fields.name: currency
fields.doc: Currency of every figure in this response.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.doc: Total spend across the window.

fields.name: groups
fields.doc: Totals per group, largest first.

fields.name: series
fields.doc: A time series, when `bucket` was supplied.

fields.name: deleted
fields.doc: How many records were removed, across every signal.

HealthStatus.doc: Whether the server is alive and able to serve.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: `ok` or `degraded`.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: The mcpd version serving this request.

fields.name: spec_version
fields.doc: The data-model spec version this build implements. A client can refuse to talk to an incompatible server.

fields.name: uptime_seconds
fields.doc: How long this process has been running.

fields.name: storage
fields.doc: Which storage backend is configured.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What is degraded, when something is.

fields.name: signup
fields.doc: True when this daemon offers open sign-up: anyone may create an account at `POST /v1/api/account/signup` and log in at `POST /v1/api/account/login`. Absent when it does not, which is the default. The interface reads this to decide whether to show its sign-up and log-in screens.

fields.name: accounts
fields.doc: True when this daemon has accounts, with or without open sign-up. Absent when it does not. The interface reads this to show its log-in screen.

fields.name: sso
fields.doc: True when at least one organisation on this daemon logs in with single sign-on, so the log-in screen offers it. Absent otherwise.

ScorerInfo.doc: One scorer mcpd can run, as described to a caller.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable identifier, recorded on every score it produces.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: What it measures, in one line.

fields.name: needs_config
fields.doc: Whether it needs settings to mean anything. A scorer that needs an expected answer cannot run without one.

ScorerConfig.doc: Settings shared by the scorers that need them. Every field is optional; a scorer that needs one and does not get it declines instead of guessing.

fields.name: needle
fields.doc: Text the answer must contain, for `contains`.

fields.name: expected
fields.doc: The expected answer, for `exact_match`.

fields.name: max_ms
fields.doc: A budget in milliseconds, for `latency_budget`.

fields.name: max_cost
fields.doc: A budget in currency units, for `cost_budget`.

fields.name: max_tool_calls
fields.doc: The most tool calls a healthy run should make, for `tool_efficiency`.

fields.name: span_kind
fields.doc: The kind of span that must be present in the run, for `span_present`.

fields.name: span_name
fields.doc: The span name that must be present in the run, for `span_present`. Matched exactly against `Span.name`.

fields.name: tool_name
fields.doc: The tool that must have run and ended `ok`, for `tool_succeeded`. Matched exactly against the `name` of a span whose kind is `tool_call`, `client_tool_call`, `provider_tool_call` or `mcp_tool_call`.

fields.name: case_sensitive
fields.doc: Case sensitivity for text comparisons.

ScoreRunRequest.doc:
A request to run scorers over runs that are already stored.

Scoring reads stored runs rather than running inline, so an evaluation can never add latency to the request it is judging, and a scorer that fails can never fail a user's request.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project's runs to score. Defaults to the server's default project.

fields.name: trace_ids
fields.doc: Score exactly these runs. Takes precedence over the window.

fields.name: from
fields.doc: Otherwise, score runs started after this time.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Most runs to score in one request, newest first, when `trace_ids` is empty. Unset, it is 100 for deterministic scorers, and for a pass with a judged scorer it is as many runs as fit in the request deadline. A judged pass that names more runs than fit, through `limit` or `trace_ids`, is refused with the cap.

fields.name: scorers
fields.doc: Which scorers to run, by id. Empty means every scorer that needs no configuration.

fields.name: config
fields.doc: Settings for the scorers that need them.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: What to record as the origin of these scores.

fields.name: dry_run
fields.doc: Report what would happen and store nothing.

SkippedScorer.doc: A scorer that declined to answer on one run.

fields.name: scorer_id
fields.doc: Which scorer declined.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: Which run it declined on.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why. Never silent: a scorer that cannot answer is more interesting than one that returned a number.

fields.name: traces_scored
fields.doc: Runs looked at.

fields.name: scores_written
fields.doc: Scores produced and stored.

fields.name: skipped
fields.doc: Every scorer that declined, with its reason.

fields.name: scores
fields.doc: The scores themselves, so the caller sees them without a second read.

ScorerDelta.doc: How one scorer moved between two experiments.

fields.name: scorer_id
fields.doc: Which scorer.

fields.name: baseline_mean
fields.doc: Mean on the baseline, when it ran there.

fields.name: baseline_n
fields.doc: Number of baseline observations.

fields.name: candidate_mean
fields.doc: Mean on the candidate.

fields.name: candidate_n
fields.doc: Number of candidate observations.

fields.name: delta
fields.doc: Candidate minus baseline.

fields.name: decidable
fields.doc: Whether the sample is large enough for the delta to mean anything. A deliberately blunt rule rather than a significance test: below twenty observations on either side, mcpd says the comparison is not decidable rather than dressing noise up as a finding.

ExperimentComparison.doc:
Two experiments, compared.

The point of an experiment is the comparison, so this reports the delta per scorer beside the sample sizes. A mean that moved on four runs is noise, and printing the counts next to it is what stops it being read as a result.

fields.name: baseline
fields.doc: The baseline's identifier.

fields.name: candidate
fields.doc: The candidate's identifier.

fields.name: scorers
fields.doc: One row per scorer present on either side.

fields.name: regressed
fields.doc: Whether any decidable scorer moved down.

CaptureRequest.doc: A request to turn stored runs into dataset cases.

fields.name: trace_ids
fields.doc: The runs to capture. Each becomes one item, keeping its trace id so anyone can go back and read what actually happened.

fields.name: use_output_as_expected
fields.doc: Record each run's own output as the expected answer. Leave this off for a run that went wrong: capturing a bad answer as the reference would enshrine the bug.

CaptureResult.doc: What a capture added to a dataset.

fields.name: captured
fields.doc: Items added.

fields.name: requested
fields.doc: Runs asked for. A gap means a run was not found.

ItemsAdded.doc: How many cases a dataset gained.

fields.name: added
fields.doc: Items added.

ErasureResult.doc: What an erasure request removed, counted per signal. The subject is not echoed back: it has been erased, and repeating it in a response that may be logged on the way out would write it down again.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project the erasure ran in. No other project was read or touched.

fields.name: traces
fields.doc: How many runs were removed.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc: How many spans were removed, with the prompts and completions they carried.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc: How many log lines were removed.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: How many metric points were removed.

fields.name: scores
fields.doc: How many scores were removed.

fields.name: feedback
fields.doc: How many pieces of feedback were removed.

fields.name: deleted
fields.doc: The total across every signal, so a caller that wants one number does not add them up.

fields.name: runs_erased
fields.doc: How many durable runs were removed from the run store, each with its step attempts, event log, deadlines, waits, the events it consumed and any span still queued for the trace store. A run is matched on the `user_id` in its correlation, as it was started with it, and removed with the whole tree of subworkflow runs it belongs to. Not part of `deleted`, which counts the trace store. Absent when this daemon does not serve runs.

fields.name: runs_in_flight
fields.doc: How many runs attributed to this person were left untouched because a run in their tree has not ended. Removing a live run would corrupt the workflow it is part of, so these are counted rather than skipped in silence, and `note` names the root runs. Cancel them, or let them end, then send the erasure again. Absent when this daemon does not serve runs.

fields.name: aspect_notes_erased
fields.doc: How many aspect notes were removed, matched by the run they describe and by the person stamped on them. Not part of `deleted`. Absent only from a store that holds no notes.

fields.name: dataset_items_erased
fields.doc: How many dataset cases captured from an erased run were emptied in place. They are not deleted, because a case was kept on purpose, so they are not part of `deleted`.

fields.name: datasets
fields.doc: The datasets those emptied cases sit in, so the reply can say where they are.

fields.name: deletes_pending
fields.doc: True when the storage backend applies the deletes after this reply is sent, as ClickHouse does, so the counts say what matched rather than what has already left the disk.

fields.name: unmatchable_identifiers
fields.doc: How many stored identifiers this request could not have matched, because they were written in the other form, hashed or plain, from the one given. A number above zero means the counts may not be the whole answer.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: Why the numbers above may not be the whole answer, in sentences an operator can repeat. Absent when they are the whole answer.

DefinitionDocument.doc: A definition as you post it: the graph, and the id and version to store it under. The body is validated at write time against `spec/definition.schema.json`; a body the walker cannot run is refused with a 400 naming the field, and unknown fields are refused, so a guard that is spelled wrong is an error and not a run that skips its guard.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The definition's identifier within its project. Matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What kind of definition. Absent means `workflow`, the only kind version 1 serves.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: The version to store the body under. Absent asks the daemon to choose: the version whose stored body is identical, or one past the highest stored. A named version that is free is taken; one held by an identical body is confirmed; one held by a different body is a 409, because a stored version never changes.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The document itself: `input_schema`, `limits`, `steps` and `output`. The definition schema names every field.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The definition's identifier.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: The version the body is stored under.

fields.name: assigned
fields.doc: True when the daemon chose the number because the body was new. False when the body already existed at this version, or you named the version yourself.

RunCursor.doc: The frontier of a run: which position in the definition's `steps` it has reached, and what sits there.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: The index into `steps`, or their count at the end of the graph.

fields.name: construct
fields.doc: What is at that position.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The step this position belongs to, when the construct has one. A fan-out names its parent step; the branch and item keys are on the attempts.

RunTimer.doc: A deadline the daemon holds for a run.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Which run.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The step the deadline belongs to. Absent for a run-level deadline.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Which deadline.

fields.name: due_at
fields.doc: When it fires.

RunWait.doc: A suspension waiting for an event.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Which run.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The `wait_event` step that is waiting.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The event name an inbound event must match.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The rendered key that picks this run out of every run waiting on that event.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When waiting stops and the node's `on_timeout` applies.

RunDetail.doc: One run and everything the daemon holds for it.

fields.name: run
fields.doc: The run.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc: Every attempt, in the order they were written.

fields.name: timers
fields.doc: The deadlines currently held. Empty once the run has ended.

fields.name: waits
fields.doc: The suspensions currently open. Empty once the run has ended.

fields.name: runs
fields.doc: The matching runs, newest first.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

RunEventPage.doc: A page of a run's event log.

fields.name: events
fields.doc: The rows after the requested sequence number, in order.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc: Whether rows beyond the last one here existed when the page was read. A run that is still moving will write more.

CauseLink.doc: One edge of a cause chain: an ancestor step, and the template path through which the step below it read that ancestor's output. An ancestor read through two paths appears twice, once per path.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The ancestor step, keyed the way the journal keys it: `refund/issue`, `classify[3]`, `poll[7]/classify`.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where the ancestor's latest attempt ended.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc: How many attempts were made at the ancestor. More than one on a step that ended `succeeded` is worth reading: it got there, but not the first time.

fields.name: template_path
fields.doc: The path as the definition writes it inside `${...}`, such as `steps.classify.output.kind`. The definition declares this edge, so the chain is read rather than inferred from timing.

fields.name: consumed_by
fields.doc: The step key that read this ancestor through `template_path`. On a direct edge it is the step the answer is about; deeper in the chain it is another ancestor.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How far this ancestor sits from the step the answer is about. `1` is read directly, `2` is read by something the step read directly, and so on.

fields.name: silent_producer
fields.doc: True when this ancestor ended `succeeded` and every step between it and the failed step ended `succeeded` too. Nothing on that path is marked failed, so no status code points at it and the value it produced is the suspect. It is not the same as `status` being `succeeded`: an ancestor sitting behind a step that did fail is not a silent producer, because that failure already explains the run.

fields.name: value_kind
fields.doc: The JSON type `template_path` resolved to on the ancestor's stored output. The value itself is never returned, only its shape. Absent when there is no output to read, which is the case for a step that never ran and for one that failed.

fields.name: value_empty
fields.doc: True when that value was null, an empty string, an empty array or an empty object. A step that ended `succeeded` and handed the step below it nothing is the failure a status code cannot catch, and this is the field that shows it. Absent for the same reason `value_kind` is.

StepCause.doc: Why one step of a run failed, answered by walking backwards along the data dependencies its definition declares. The daemon reads the run journal and the pinned definition version, both of which it has to hold to render `${...}` templates at all, so this answer is available with span payload capture off and with no model, prompt or completion involved.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: The run this answer is about.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The step this answer is about, as it was asked for.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where that step's latest attempt ended.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc: How many attempts were made at it.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why the latest attempt failed, when it did. Absent on a step that did not fail, because the endpoint answers for any step, not only a failed one.

fields.name: chain
fields.doc: The ancestors whose output this step consumed, directly or transitively. Ordered by `depth` ascending, then by the order the paths appear in the definition, so two calls against one run return the same list in the same order. Empty when the step reads nothing but the run input.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: True when the walk stopped at `max_depth` with ancestors left unvisited, so `chain` is a prefix of the answer rather than the whole of it.

StartRunRequest.doc: A request to start a run.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

fields.name: definition_id
fields.doc: Which definition to run.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: Which version. Absent pins the highest stored version at this moment, and the run records it.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: The run's input. Validated against the definition's `input_schema` when it declares one; a failure is a 400.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Context to store on the run and copy onto every span the daemon writes for it. `project` and `run_id` inside it are ignored: the run's own values win.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc: Makes the start idempotent per project for 24 hours: a repost returns the same run and starts nothing, and two simultaneous posts of one key produce one run.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

fields.name: worker_id
fields.doc: Who is asking. Recorded on the attempt as `lease_owner` and in the run's event log. Nothing else about the worker is stored.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: The most leases to hand back, 1 to 100.

fields.name: wait_ms
fields.doc: How long to hold the request open waiting for work, 0 to 60000 milliseconds. The daemon holds a claim for at most four fifths of its request timeout, 24000 at the default 30 seconds, so a longer wait is answered early rather than cut off with a 503. An empty answer means nothing became runnable in time: reissue the claim.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Restrict the claim to one run, which is how a script drives its own run inline.

StepLease.doc: A step handed to a worker. Every later call about the attempt is addressed by `lease_id`.

fields.name: lease_id
fields.doc: The address of every later call about this attempt.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Which run.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project the run belongs to.

fields.name: definition_id
fields.doc: Which definition the run is executing.

fields.name: definition_version
fields.doc: Which version. Fail the lease with class `unservable` if you do not serve it.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: The step to run. A worker that does not recognise it fails the lease with class `unservable` rather than guessing.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Whether this is a plain task or an agent turn.

fields.name: attempt
fields.doc: Which attempt this is. The fence: a call about this lease is refused once a later attempt exists.

fields.name: effect
fields.doc: Under `at_most_once`, post `started` and wait for its 200 before running the body.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When the lease lapses. Heartbeat every `heartbeat_ms` to keep it.

fields.name: deadline_ms
fields.doc: The step's own timeout, when the node declares one. It bounds the attempt whatever the heartbeats say.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc: A key stable across every attempt of this step: the SHA-256 of `run_id:step_key`. Pass it to any downstream call that can deduplicate.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: The node's `input` template rendered for this attempt, or the run's input when the node declares none.

fields.name: prior
fields.doc: The ended attempts of earlier steps, keyed by step id: `{ status, output?, error? }` for the latest attempt of each, or `{ status: skipped }`. Only ended attempts appear.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The run's state object as it stands.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: The run's correlation, with `run_id` set. Put it on every span you record inside this step.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The run's trace. Set it on every span you record inside this step.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The span the daemon has already opened for this attempt. Set it as `parent_span_id` on your own spans, so a model call or a tool call nests under the step.

fields.name: parent_span_id
fields.doc: The run's root span, which this attempt's span hangs off.

fields.name: leases
fields.doc: Zero to `max` leases. Empty when nothing became runnable within `wait_ms`.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: The lease's new expiry.

fields.name: reclaimed
fields.doc: True when this call found the attempt `orphaned` and restored it to the state it came from.

StepUsage.doc: Token usage a worker reports on `complete`. The daemon prices it from its price book and charges the attempt, the run and the root of the run tree.

fields.name: input_tokens
fields.doc: Total input tokens.

fields.name: output_tokens
fields.doc: Total output tokens.

fields.name: total_tokens
fields.doc: Input plus output, when the provider reports a total that differs from the sum.

fields.name: input_details
fields.doc: How the input tokens were billed.

fields.name: output_details
fields.doc: How the output tokens were billed.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: The model that produced the usage, which the price book needs to price it.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: The provider that served the model.

StepResult.doc: What a worker posts to complete a step.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: The step's output. Later steps read it as `steps.<id>.output`.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: An object to merge shallowly into the run's state.

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: Token usage to price and charge.

StepError.doc: Why a step failed, as the worker reports it.

fields.name: class
fields.doc: What kind of failure. Decides whether the daemon retries.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What went wrong, for the person reading the run.

fields.name: details
fields.doc: Structured detail. Stored on the attempt.

fields.name: retry_after_ms
fields.doc: The least the daemon should wait before the next attempt, when the worker knows: a rate limit's reset, say. Honoured when it is larger than the backoff. At most 315360000000 (3650 days), the bound on every duration in a definition; a larger value is a 400 naming this field.

StepFailure.doc: What a worker posts to fail a step.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed.

fields.name: run_status
fields.doc: Where the run is after this call.

fields.name: next
fields.doc: `claim` when more work is runnable now, `idle` otherwise.

fields.name: attempts_left
fields.doc: After a `fail`: how many attempts the node's retry budget still allows.

StepConflict.doc: The body of a 409 from a worker call. `reason` says what is true and what the worker should do next.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Always `conflict`.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Which conflict.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The reason, in words.

fields.name: attempt
fields.doc: The attempt the lease addressed.

fields.name: attempt_status
fields.doc: Where that attempt is, when it still exists. Under `already_applied` this says how the step ended.

fields.name: run_status
fields.doc: Where the run is.

PublishEventRequest.doc: An event for whichever run is waiting for it.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The event name, matched against open waits.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: Matched against the rendered `key` of each waiting run. Delivered to the matching run whose wait expires soonest.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Becomes the waiting step's output.

fields.name: event_id
fields.doc: Your own id for this event. A supplied id seen before answers `duplicate` and writes nothing, whether or not a run is waiting. Absent, the daemon derives one from `project`, `event`, `key` and `payload`, and a derived id counts as a duplicate only when no run is waiting, because two identical approvals for two runs on one key are two events. Send your own id from any handler that can be retried.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: Delivered, parked or duplicate.

fields.name: event_id
fields.doc: The id used, supplied or derived.

SignalRequest.doc: An event for one run, addressed by run id rather than by key. The daemon reads the run's open wait on `event`, takes its key, and routes the event as a published one.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The event name. The run must hold an open wait on it.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Becomes the waiting step's output.

fields.name: event_id
fields.doc: Your own id for this event, deduplicated as on a published event.

WorkerRegistration.doc: A worker announcing the definitions it serves.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project. A selector: refused with 403 on a mismatch with the key's grant, filled in for a single-project key, and a 400 when a multi-project key names none.

fields.name: worker_id
fields.doc: Who is registering. Not stored: dispatch reads the runnable set, never a worker table.

fields.name: definitions
fields.doc: Each is stored under the versioning rule, exactly as if posted to the definitions endpoint.

fields.name: worker_id
fields.doc: The id you registered with.

fields.name: registered
fields.doc: Where each definition landed, in the order posted.

fields.name: lease_ttl_ms
fields.doc: How long a lease lasts without a heartbeat.

fields.name: heartbeat_ms
fields.doc: How often to heartbeat a held lease: a third of `lease_ttl_ms`.

Monitor.doc: A saved condition the daemon evaluates on a schedule. Monitors are configured in the daemon's configuration file, not through the API.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable identifier.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What a person should read when it trips.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project it watches.

fields.name: watch
fields.doc: What it measures.

fields.name: scorer_id
fields.doc: Which scorer, when `watch` is `score_mean`.

fields.name: compare
fields.doc: Which direction trips it.

fields.name: threshold
fields.doc: The threshold.

fields.name: window_seconds
fields.doc: How far back each evaluation looks.

fields.name: min_samples
fields.doc: The fewest runs the window must contain before the monitor will trip. Without it a single failed run in a quiet hour is a 100% error rate, and the first thing anyone does with an alert that cries wolf is mute it.

fields.name: webhook
fields.doc: Where to POST when it trips or clears. Set as a full URL in the config file; the API returns only its host, because a webhook URL is often its own credential.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether it is evaluated at all.

fields.name: monitor_id
fields.doc: Which monitor.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: When it was evaluated.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The measured value, when there was enough data to measure one.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: How many runs the window held.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: The resulting condition.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What a person should read.

MonitorState.doc: A monitor and the condition it is latched in.

fields.name: monitor
fields.doc: The monitor.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: Its current condition.

fields.name: last
fields.doc: The most recent reading. Absent before the first evaluation.

fields.name: tripped_at
fields.doc: When it first tripped, while it stays tripped.

Slo.doc: A service level objective: the fraction of runs that must succeed over a window. A monitor asks whether a number is over a line right now. An objective asks whether the promise is going to be missed and how fast the error budget is burning, over two windows at once, so a two minute blip and a slow leak get the different answers they need. Objectives are configured in the daemon's configuration file, not through the API.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable identifier.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What a person should read.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project it covers.

fields.name: objective
fields.doc: The fraction of runs that must succeed, between 0 and 1. `0.995` is ninety-nine and a half percent of runs.

fields.name: window_days
fields.doc: How long the promise is measured over.

fields.name: min_samples
fields.doc: The fewest runs a burn window must hold before it may trip.

fields.name: webhook
fields.doc: Where to POST on a transition. Set as a full URL in the config file; the API returns only its host, because a webhook URL is often its own credential.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether it is evaluated at all.

fields.name: slo_id
fields.doc: Which objective.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: When it was evaluated.

fields.name: success_rate
fields.doc: The observed success rate over the whole window.

fields.name: budget_remaining
fields.doc: The fraction of the error budget still unspent. Negative once it is overspent, which says by how much the promise was missed.

fields.name: burn_fast
fields.doc: The burn rate over the one hour window. A rate of 1 spends the whole budget exactly over the whole window.

fields.name: burn_slow
fields.doc: The burn rate over the six hour window. Both windows must exceed their trip rate together before the objective trips, which is what stops a brief spike paging anyone.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: Runs in the whole window.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: The resulting condition.

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: What a person should read.

SloState.doc: An objective and the condition it is latched in.

fields.name: slo
fields.doc: The objective.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc: Its current condition.

fields.name: last
fields.doc: The most recent reading. Absent before the first evaluation.

fields.name: tripped_at
fields.doc: When it first tripped, while it stays tripped.

StoreCapabilities.doc: What the storage backend behind this daemon can and cannot do. Three backends implement one storage trait and they are not equal: a reader on ClickHouse who searches for `CAFE` with an acute and finds nothing has no way to learn that this backend folds ASCII case and no more. Read this once at connect time and offer only what the deployment answers. Every field is named after the capability an endpoint names when it refuses with 501, so the two can be compared without translation.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Which backend this describes: `sqlite`, `postgres` or `clickhouse`. The same string `/healthz` reports as `storage`.

fields.name: text_search
fields.doc: What the `q` parameter matches.

fields.name: unicode_case_folding
fields.doc: Whether `q` folds case for letters outside ASCII. False means a search for `CAFE` with an acute does not find the lowercase form, which a reader otherwise meets as an empty result they cannot explain.

fields.name: immediate_deletes
fields.doc: Whether a delete is on disk when the call returns. False means the backend accepted the delete and applies it afterwards, so a count says what matched rather than what has already gone.

fields.name: discovery
fields.doc: Whether `GET /v1/api/discovery` answers. False means a filter box has to be filled from what is already on screen.

fields.name: discovery_label_values
fields.doc: Whether the `metric_label_value` facet is answerable, not only the keys. Separate because the values are the expensive half: a key set is small and bounded, and a value set is not.

fields.name: delta_polling
fields.doc: Whether `GET /v1/api/deltas` answers, so a list refreshes from a cursor rather than by running the whole query again.

fields.name: per_signal_retention
fields.doc: Whether retention can carry a different window per signal. False means one window covers all five.

fields.name: declarative_retention
fields.doc: Whether the window can be handed to the database engine, so nothing has to run a delete on a timer.

fields.name: partitioning
fields.doc: How the signal tables are cut on their anchor time.

fields.name: partition_drop_retention
fields.doc: Whether a retention pass can drop a whole partition instead of deleting rows one at a time.

fields.name: idempotent_schema_init
fields.doc: Whether a start with nothing to apply issues no schema statement at all. False means every process replays the schema on every boot, which is harmless on one node and is metadata churn across a replicated deployment.

fields.name: theme_analysis
fields.doc: Whether this deployment answers the Intelligence endpoints. False means the store holds no note or theme tables and every one of those routes refuses with 501 naming this capability, so a client decides once whether to offer the feature rather than showing a reader an empty page they cannot account for. Every backend that answers gives the same themes: the clustering runs in the daemon over stored notes and not in SQL, so there is nothing here for a backend to do differently.

DiscoveredValue.doc: One value a filter dimension takes in a project.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The value, exactly as it is stored, so it can be sent straight back as a filter with no further mapping.

fields.name: last_seen
fields.doc: When mcpd last received a signal carrying it. This is arrival time and not the signal's own timestamp, so a backfill of last year's data does not make a value look current. Carried so a caller can rank down or grey out a value nothing has reported for a month. Values are ordered by `value` and not by this: a list somebody reads alphabetically is stable between polls, and one ordered by recency reshuffles under them as data arrives.

DiscoveryResponse.doc: The values one filter dimension takes, for a filter box. Answered from a distinct-value list the daemon maintains as signals arrive, not by scanning the signal tables, because the question is asked on every keystroke and the tables it would otherwise scan are the largest thing the deployment holds.

fields.name: facet
fields.doc: Which dimension was asked for.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The label key the values belong to, echoed back for `metric_label_value`. Absent for every other facet.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: The values, ordered by value, ascending.

DeltaResponse.doc: What has arrived since a cursor. A poll is not a page: paging walks a fixed result set backwards in the sort you chose, and polling walks forwards in arrival order and never ends, so the two cursors are different things and are deliberately not interchangeable. Rows come back oldest arrival first, so applying them in order to a list you already hold gives the same result as having listed afresh.

fields.name: signal
fields.doc: Which signal these rows are. Exactly one of the three arrays below is present, and it is this one.

fields.name: cursor
