fields.doc: Where the next poll resumes. Always present, and unchanged from the request when nothing came back: moving it forward on an empty poll is what would drop a row that lands a moment later with an earlier arrival time. Treat it as meaningless, and send back the one you were given.

fields.name: has_more
fields.doc: True when the page filled and more is waiting, so a caller draining a backlog polls again at once rather than waiting for its next tick.

fields.name: traces
fields.doc: The runs that arrived, when `signal` is `traces`.

fields.name: spans
fields.doc: The steps that arrived, when `signal` is `spans`.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc: The log lines that arrived, when `signal` is `logs`.

AspectLimits.doc: The bounds a clustering pass runs under. They are published because each one changes what a reader is looking at: a floor that has not been reached means no themes at all rather than an empty result, and a ceiling that has been reached means every share is a share of what was read. They are copied from the divergence watch, which is the one windowed statistic mcpd already ships. `pass_armed` is the first of them to read: the other three describe what a pass would do, and it says whether one runs.

fields.name: min_notes_to_cluster
fields.doc: How many notes one aspect on one entity needs before a pass runs at all, 50 by default. Below it the aspect reads `collecting` and no snapshot is written.

fields.name: max_notes_per_pass
fields.doc: The most notes one pass reads, 20,000 by default, taken newest first. A window holding more is clustered from the newest of them and its snapshot is marked `capped`.

fields.name: page_size
fields.doc: How many notes the pass reads at a time while it fills a window, 500 by default. It bounds what the pass holds, not what it covers.

fields.name: max_aspects
fields.doc: How many aspects one project may define, the four built-ins included. It is configuration and is published here so a client that lets an operator add an aspect knows when to stop instead of finding out from a refusal.

fields.name: pass_armed
fields.doc: Whether this deployment runs the clustering pass at all. False means no snapshot will ever be written however many notes arrive, so every aspect stays `collecting` or `processing` for ever and no theme route will have anything to answer with. It is configuration and not a fault, and it is not the same thing as the 501 the theme routes give: that says the storage backend cannot hold the tables, which nobody can switch on, while this says nobody has switched the pass on yet. It is published here rather than on every progress row because it is one fact about the deployment, and a client reads this route once to learn what the aspects are called.

AspectCatalogue.doc: Every aspect a project describes traces along, with the bounds the clustering pass runs under. The four built-ins are rows in the same table as anything you define, so there is no fallback list inside a client that can quietly disagree with this one.

fields.name: aspects
fields.doc: The aspects, in `sort_order`. Disabled aspects are included, because notes already recorded under one stay readable and a name that vanished from this list would make them look like a mistake.

fields.name: limits
fields.doc: The bounds a pass runs under in this deployment.

EntityIndexRow.doc: One entity that has aspect notes, with the roll-up a list needs to be worth reading. A row appears as soon as the first note is recorded, before any theme exists, because an empty screen with a count moving on it is a different thing from an empty screen and a reader has to be able to tell them apart.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.doc: The kind of thing this row is about.

fields.name: entity_name
fields.doc: Its name.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many of its traces carry at least one note. This is not the entity's trace count: writing a note lags ingestion, so a busy agent can show far fewer here.

fields.name: note_count
fields.doc: How many notes are recorded about it.

fields.name: enabled_aspects
fields.doc: How many aspects are switched on for this entity's project.

fields.name: ready_aspects
fields.doc: How many of those have themes to read. The two numbers read as `2 of 4` and are the honest answer to whether this row is worth opening yet.

fields.name: readiness
fields.doc: The row's overall state, which is the least advanced of its enabled aspects, so a row says `processing` while any one of them is still short of a snapshot. It never reports the best case.

fields.name: last_note_at
fields.doc: When the newest note about this entity was recorded, so a reader can tell a list that is filling from one that stopped.

fields.name: latest_snapshot_at
fields.doc: The cutoff of this entity's newest snapshot. Absent until a pass has written one, which is the ordinary state of a row that is still collecting.

EntityIndexResponse.doc: A page of the entities that have aspect notes.

fields.name: entities
fields.doc: The matching entities, most recently written to first.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

AspectProgressRow.doc: How far one aspect has got for one entity. Counted from stored notes, so it is what has happened and not a projection of what will.

fields.name: aspect
fields.doc: Which aspect this row is about.

fields.name: readiness
fields.doc: The state this aspect is in for this entity.

fields.name: note_count
fields.doc: How many notes are recorded along it.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

fields.name: notes_needed
fields.doc: How many more notes this aspect needs before a pass will run. Zero once the floor is reached, which is what turns a wait into a number a reader can watch.

fields.name: last_note_at
fields.doc: When the newest note along this aspect was recorded. Absent when there are none.

AspectProgress.doc: What the daemon has recorded for one entity, aspect by aspect. This is the answer to why a themes screen is empty, and it separates the three cases that look identical on screen: nothing has been recorded, enough has been recorded and no pass has run yet, or there are themes to read and the reader is looking at the wrong aspect.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.doc: The kind of entity this describes.

fields.name: entity_name
fields.doc: Its name.

fields.name: readiness
fields.doc: The entity's overall state, which is the least advanced of its enabled aspects.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many of this entity's traces carry at least one note.

fields.name: aspects
fields.doc: One row per enabled aspect, in catalogue order.

fields.name: latest_snapshot
fields.doc: The newest snapshot for this entity, when a pass has written one. Absent while every aspect is still collecting.

SnapshotLandmark.doc: One snapshot in a timeline, with the reason it was chosen.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: The snapshot.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why this snapshot is in the selection. Present for `presentation=landmarks` only; an inventory returns consecutive snapshots and chooses nothing, so there is nothing to report.

SnapshotListResponse.doc: A selection of one entity's snapshots, oldest first, so a timeline can be drawn without reordering anything.

fields.name: snapshots
fields.doc: The selected snapshots, oldest first.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: How many snapshots the entity has in the requested range. This is the number the selection was drawn from and not the number returned, so a timeline can say what it is standing in for.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

ThemeNode.doc: One node of one stage of a flow: a theme, the stage's noise, or the overflow the stage folded away.

fields.name: node_id
fields.doc: Identifies this node inside this flow, and is what a link names at either end. It is not a theme id: the noise and overflow nodes have one of these and no theme id.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Whether this node is a theme, the noise or the overflow.

fields.name: theme_id
fields.doc: The theme this node stands for. Present only when `kind` is `theme`, which is what makes the other two impossible to drill into by accident.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: What to show for this node: a theme's own label, or the words for noise or overflow.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many traces this node accounts for.

fields.name: coverage
fields.doc: This node's share of the stage's traces, between 0 and 1. A stage's nodes cover all of it, so its shares add to 1.

ThemeStage.doc: One aspect's column in a flow. Stages come back in the order the aspects were asked for, and links only ever join neighbouring stages, so the order decides which co-occurrences are visible and is not a display preference.

fields.name: aspect
fields.doc: Which aspect this stage is.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many traces this stage accounts for.

fields.name: nodes
fields.doc: The stage's nodes, largest first, with the noise and overflow nodes last.

ThemeLink.doc: A ribbon between one node of a stage and one node of the next. It says the two describe the same traces and nothing more: a link between a goal theme and an outcome theme means they were written about the same runs, not that one caused the other.

fields.name: source_node_id
fields.doc: The node this link leaves, in the earlier stage.

fields.name: target_node_id
fields.doc: The node it reaches, in the next stage.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many traces are assigned to both ends.

fields.name: source_share
fields.doc: That count as a fraction of the source node's traces, between 0 and 1.

fields.name: target_share
fields.doc: That count as a fraction of the target node's traces, between 0 and 1. The two shares differ whenever the nodes are different sizes, and reading only one of them is how a thin ribbon gets mistaken for a weak relationship.

ThemeFlow.doc: One snapshot read across two to four aspects at once: a stage per aspect, and the links between neighbouring stages. Association, never causation.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: The snapshot this flow was computed from, so every count on the page can be read against the window it came from.

fields.name: stages
fields.doc: One stage per aspect, in the order they were asked for.

fields.name: links
fields.doc: The links between neighbouring stages. There are none between stages that are not neighbours, which is why the order of the aspects matters.

ThemeDetail.doc: One theme in one snapshot, or the answer that this snapshot did not hold it.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.doc: The snapshot that was read, with its own counts, so a caller can write `28 of 70 traces in this window` without a second request.

fields.name: theme
fields.doc: The theme, when this snapshot holds it. Absent is an answer and not an error: the theme did not exist in that window, which is what scrubbing a timeline back past a theme's birth looks like. A theme id this entity has never had is a 404 instead.

ThemeExample.doc: One note from a theme, with the run it was written about. The two ids are different things: `note_id` identifies the sentence and `trace_id` identifies the run it describes.

fields.name: note_id
fields.doc: The note this example is.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace the note was written about.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The sentence, after redaction. This is the wording that put the trace in this theme, so a reader can see why it landed here rather than take it on trust.

fields.name: similarity
fields.doc: How much this note's wording overlaps the theme's label, counted out of 64. It is a count of shared sketch positions and not a percentage, and it is an integer on purpose: no part of the clustering uses floating-point arithmetic, so two replicas cannot order the same notes differently.

fields.name: trace_started_at
fields.doc: When the run began, so examples can be read against the period they came from rather than against when the note was written.

ThemeExampleListResponse.doc: A page of the notes behind one theme.

fields.name: examples
fields.doc: The notes, most like the theme's label first.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

ThemeHistoryPoint.doc: One theme in one snapshot of its life. Every count belongs to that snapshot alone, and windows overlap, so a run of these is read as a series and never added up.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.doc: The snapshot this point comes from.

fields.name: cutoff_at
fields.doc: When that snapshot became the current state.

fields.name: window_from
fields.doc: Start of that snapshot's window, inclusive.

fields.name: window_to
fields.doc: End of that snapshot's window, exclusive.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: What had happened to the theme by this point.

fields.name: note_count
fields.doc: How many notes were in the theme here.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

fields.name: coverage
fields.doc: The theme's share of the notes that snapshot read for this aspect, between 0 and 1. Coverage and raw count can move in opposite directions, and coverage is the one that says whether a theme is gaining ground.

fields.name: split_from
fields.doc: The themes this one came out of at this point. Empty unless `state` is `split`.

fields.name: split_into
fields.doc: The themes that came out of this one at this point. Both directions are stored, so a caller never has to read a second theme's history to learn what happened to this one.

fields.name: merged_from
fields.doc: The themes that became this one at this point. Empty unless `state` is `merge`.

fields.name: merged_into
fields.doc: The theme this one became at this point, when it stopped being its own theme.

ThemeHistory.doc: One theme across every stored snapshot that holds it, oldest first. This is the only theme response that names no single snapshot, because the series is the answer.

fields.name: theme_id
fields.doc: The theme this history is of.

fields.name: aspect
fields.doc: The aspect it was clustered along.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The theme's label at its newest point. A label can change between snapshots, because the note most like the others can change while the theme holds together.

fields.name: points
fields.doc: The series, oldest first, so nothing has to be reordered before it is drawn or differenced.

fields.name: page
fields.doc: Cursor and totals.

TraceAspectNotes.doc: Every aspect note recorded about one trace, which is at most one per aspect. Read it beside the trace itself: a note is the sentence that put this run in each of its themes, so it is the shortest route from a theme back to what actually happened.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace these notes are about.

fields.name: notes
fields.doc: The notes, in catalogue order. Empty when nothing has written one yet, which is ordinary for a recent trace.

AccountCredentials.doc: An email address and a password, for sign-up and for log-in.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The account's email address. Compared without regard to case, and with surrounding spaces removed.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes. Stored only as an argon2id hash.

fields.name: totp_code
fields.doc: The six-digit code from an authenticator app, or one of the recovery codes, when the account has two-step log-in on. Ignored by sign-up.

AccountSession.doc: A logged-in session. Send `token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The session token. It is shown once: the daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When the session stops working. Log in again after this.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The account's email address, as stored.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project reads go to when they name none. The account's own project, or the first project of the organisation a single sign-on session is limited to. Absent when the session reaches no project yet.

fields.name: org_id
fields.doc: Set when the session came from an organisation's single sign-on. The session then reaches that organisation's projects only.

Account.doc: The account a session belongs to.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The account's email address, as stored.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project created with the account at sign-up. Absent for an account that was invited, or created by single sign-on or SCIM.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the account was created.

fields.name: email_verified
fields.doc: Whether the address has been confirmed by a link sent to it.

fields.name: totp_enabled
fields.doc: Whether two-step log-in is on.

fields.name: has_password
fields.doc: Whether the account can log in with a password. False for an account created by single sign-on or SCIM that has never set one.

fields.name: managed_by
fields.doc: The organisation that created this account through single sign-on or SCIM. That organisation can deactivate it.

AccountKey.doc: One API key an account holds. The secret is not part of it: the daemon keeps only a digest.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The key's identifier, for revoking it. Not a secret.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What the key may do.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The one project the key reaches.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The label given when the key was created.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: The first characters of the secret, so you can tell which key a process holds without the daemon storing the secret.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the key was created.

fields.name: created_by
fields.doc: The email of the account that created the key. Set in an organisation's key list, so an admin can see whose key it is.

CreateAccountKeyRequest.doc: A request for a new API key.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What the key may do. One scope per key.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: A label for the key, such as the service that will hold it. At most 100 characters.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project the key reaches. Defaults to the account's own project. Your role on the project must allow the scope.

CreatedAccountKey.doc: A new API key, with its secret. This is the only time the secret is shown.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: The key as it is listed from now on.

fields.name: secret
fields.doc: The key itself. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. Copy it now: the daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest and cannot show it again.

AccountNotice.doc: A plain answer that changes nothing you can read back, such as "check your email".

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What happened, and what to do next.

TokenRequest.doc: A one-time token from a link the daemon sent by email.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The token, as it appears in the link.

PasswordForgotRequest.doc: A request for a password reset link.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The address to send the link to. The answer is the same whether or not an account uses it.

PasswordResetRequest.doc: A new password, with the token from a reset link.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The token from the reset link. It works once, for one hour.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: The new password. At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes.

fields.name: totp_code
fields.doc: A code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code, when the account has two-step log-in on. A reset proves the address, not the second factor.

PasswordChangeRequest.doc: A new password for the logged-in account.

fields.name: current_password
fields.doc: The password in use now. Required when the account has one.

fields.name: new_password
fields.doc: The new password. At least 10 characters and at most 1024 bytes.

EmailChangeRequest.doc: A new email address for the logged-in account.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The new address. A link is sent to it, and the change happens when the link is opened.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

AccountDeleteRequest.doc: Confirmation for deleting the logged-in account.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

fields.name: totp_code
fields.doc: A code from the authenticator app. Required when two-step log-in is on.

fields.name: orgs_deleted
fields.doc: Organisations that had this account as their only member, deleted with it.

fields.name: projects_erased
fields.doc: Projects whose stored signals and runs were erased, because their organisation was deleted.

SessionInfo.doc: One live session of the logged-in account. The token is not part of it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The session's identifier, for ending it. Not a secret.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the session started.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When it stops working.

fields.name: current
fields.doc: True for the session this request carries.

fields.name: via
fields.doc: How it started: `password`, `sso`, `invite`, `verify` or `reset`.

fields.name: org_id
fields.doc: The organisation a single sign-on session is limited to.

fields.name: user_agent
fields.doc: The browser or client that started it, as it described itself.

fields.name: address
fields.doc: The client address that started it.

TotpSetup.doc: A new authenticator secret, not yet in use. Confirm it with a code to turn two-step log-in on.

fields.name: secret
fields.doc: The secret in base32, for typing into an authenticator app.

fields.name: otpauth_uri
fields.doc: The same secret as an `otpauth://` URI.

fields.name: qr_svg
fields.doc: The URI as a QR code, an SVG document.

TotpCodeRequest.doc: A code from an authenticator app.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The six-digit code.

fields.name: recovery_codes
fields.doc: Ten single-use codes that stand in for the authenticator app. They are shown once: the daemon keeps only their digests.

TotpDisableRequest.doc: Confirmation for turning two-step log-in off.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: The account's password. Required when the account has one.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: A code from the authenticator app, or a recovery code.

Org.doc: An organisation: the owner of projects, members and single sign-on settings.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The organisation's identifier.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its display name.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: Your role in it.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created.

fields.name: quota_per_minute
fields.doc: The most signals all its projects together may store per minute. Absent means no ceiling.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.doc: How long its projects keep data, in days. Absent means forever.

fields.name: members
fields.doc: How many members it has.

fields.name: projects
fields.doc: How many projects it owns.

fields.name: managed_by_config
fields.doc: True when the daemon's configuration file declares this organisation. Its single sign-on settings are then read from that file and cannot be changed here.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Its display name, at most 100 characters.

UpdateOrgRequest.doc: Changes to an organisation. A field left out keeps its value.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: A new display name, at most 100 characters.

fields.name: quota_per_minute
fields.doc: A ceiling on signals per minute across all the organisation's projects, at most the daemon's own ceiling. 0 restores the daemon's default. Owner only.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.doc: How long to keep data, in days, at most the daemon's own window. 0 restores the daemon's default. Owner only.

fields.name: projects_erased
fields.doc: Projects whose stored signals and runs were erased.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role there.

fields.name: account_id
fields.doc: The member's account.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The member's email address.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The member's role.

fields.name: via
fields.doc: How they joined: `created`, `invite`, `sso`, `scim` or `config`.

fields.name: joined_at
fields.doc: When they joined.

fields.name: project_roles
fields.doc: Roles on single projects that replace the organisation role there.

fields.name: managed
fields.doc: True when this organisation created the account through single sign-on or SCIM.

fields.name: totp_enabled
fields.doc: Whether the member has two-step log-in on.

UpdateMemberRequest.doc: A new role for a member.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role. Only an owner may grant or remove `owner`, and the last owner cannot be demoted.

SetProjectRoleRequest.doc: A role for a member on one project.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: A project the organisation owns.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role there. Absent removes the project role, so the organisation role applies again.

OrgInvite.doc: An invitation not yet accepted. The token is not part of it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: The invitation's identifier, for revoking it.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The address it was sent to.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role it grants.

fields.name: project_roles
fields.doc: Project roles it grants as well.

fields.name: invited_by
fields.doc: The email of the member who sent it. Absent when the configuration file or SCIM sent it.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was sent.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When it stops working.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: Who to invite. The link is sent to this address.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role to grant. Only an owner may invite an owner.

fields.name: project_roles
fields.doc: Project roles to grant as well.

InviteLookup.doc: What an invitation offers, read with its token before accepting it.

fields.name: org_name
fields.doc: The organisation.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: The address it was sent to. Accepting it joins the account with this address.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role it grants.

fields.name: account_exists
fields.doc: Whether an account with this address exists. If it does, log in as it to accept; if not, accepting creates it.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When it stops working.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The token from the invitation link.

fields.name: password
fields.doc: A password for the new account, when no account uses the invited address. Ignored otherwise.

fields.name: org
fields.doc: The organisation joined.

fields.name: session
fields.doc: A session for the account accepting created. Absent when an existing account accepted with its own session.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project name. Random, so nobody can choose one that already holds somebody else's data.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A display label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created or attached.

CreateProjectRequest.doc: A new project in an organisation.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A display label, at most 100 characters.

OrgUsage.doc: How much an organisation is using, against its ceilings. Counted since the daemon started.

fields.name: org_id
fields.doc: The organisation.

fields.name: quota_per_minute
fields.doc: Its ceiling on signals per minute, when it has one.

fields.name: admitted_this_minute
fields.doc: Signals stored in the current one-minute window.

fields.name: admitted_total
fields.doc: Signals stored since the daemon started.

fields.name: refused_total
fields.doc: Signals refused for the ceiling since the daemon started.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.doc: How long its projects keep data, in days.

fields.name: members
fields.doc: Members.

fields.name: projects
fields.doc: Projects.

fields.name: keys
fields.doc: API keys on its projects.

fields.name: since
fields.doc: When counting started.

SsoConfig.doc: An organisation's single sign-on settings. The client secret is not part of it.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: The kind of provider.

fields.name: issuer
fields.doc: The OpenID Connect issuer URL. Absent for GitHub.

fields.name: client_id
fields.doc: The client id registered with the provider.

fields.name: has_client_secret
fields.doc: Whether a client secret is stored.

fields.name: domains
fields.doc: Email domains this organisation claims. Single sign-on creates accounts only for these domains, and "Log in with SSO" finds the organisation by them.

fields.name: enforced
fields.doc: When true, members whose email is in a claimed domain cannot log in with a password.

fields.name: default_role
fields.doc: The role given to a member single sign-on creates, when no group maps to a role. Never `owner`.

fields.name: groups_claim
fields.doc: The ID token claim that lists the member's groups, mapped to roles by the group roles.

fields.name: redirect_url
fields.doc: The redirect URL to register with the provider.

fields.name: managed_by_config
fields.doc: True when these settings come from the configuration file.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc: When they were last changed.

PutSsoConfigRequest.doc: New single sign-on settings for an organisation.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: The kind of provider.

fields.name: issuer
fields.doc: The OpenID Connect issuer URL, such as `https://accounts.google.com`. Required for `oidc`. Must be `https`.

fields.name: client_id
fields.doc: The client id registered with the provider.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.doc: The client secret. Left out, the stored one is kept.

fields.name: domains
fields.doc: Email domains to claim. You can claim the domain of your own verified address. A domain belongs to one organisation.

fields.name: enforced
fields.doc: Refuse password log-in for members in the claimed domains. Turning it on ends their password sessions.

fields.name: default_role
fields.doc: The role for a member single sign-on creates. `admin`, `member` or `viewer`.

fields.name: groups_claim
fields.doc: The ID token claim that lists groups, such as `groups`.

GroupRole.doc: A group from the identity provider, and the role its members get.

fields.name: group
fields.doc: The group name, as single sign-on or SCIM sends it. Compared without regard to case.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: The role. Never `owner`.

ScimTokenInfo.doc: Whether an organisation has a SCIM token. The token is not part of it.

fields.name: configured
fields.doc: Whether a token exists.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: The first characters of the token.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc: The SCIM base URL to give your identity provider.

CreatedScimToken.doc: A new SCIM token. This is the only time it is shown, and it replaces any earlier token.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The bearer token for your identity provider. The daemon keeps only its SHA-256 digest.

fields.name: prefix
fields.doc: Its first characters.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created.

fields.name: base_url
fields.doc: The SCIM base URL to give your identity provider.

SsoStartRequest.doc: Where to start single sign-on. Give one of the two.

fields.name: email
fields.doc: Your email address. Its domain finds the organisation.

fields.name: org_id
fields.doc: The organisation, when you know it.

SsoStart.doc: Where to send the browser for single sign-on.

fields.name: authorize_url
fields.doc: The provider's authorization URL, with state, nonce and the PKCE challenge in it.

fields.name: binding
fields.doc: A secret to keep in this browser and send back with the callback. It ties the callback to the browser that started it, so a link from somebody else cannot log you in as them.

fields.name: org_name
fields.doc: The organisation.

SsoCallbackRequest.doc: What the provider sent back to the redirect URL.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: The `state` parameter.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The `code` parameter.

fields.name: binding
fields.doc: The binding from the start of the flow.

Span.doc: One unit of work. Spans are the backbone of mcpd: logs, metrics, scores and feedback all hang off a span or a trace.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: 128-bit trace id, 32 lowercase hex characters. OpenTelemetry-compatible.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: 64-bit span id, 16 lowercase hex characters. Unique within the trace.

fields.name: parent_span_id
fields.doc: The parent span within this trace. Absent on the root.

fields.name: external_parent_span_id
fields.doc: A parent from a foreign tracing system that mcpd did not create. Carried for correlation, never used for mcpd's own tree.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What this operation is called. Keep it low-cardinality: `search_docs`, not `search_docs(query=hello)`.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What kind of operation this is.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The outcome.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: When the operation began, in UTC with nanosecond precision.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: When it finished. Absent while the span is still running.

fields.name: duration_ns
fields.doc: Derived from the timestamps at ingest, stored so the database never has to compute it to sort.

fields.name: is_root
fields.doc: True when this span has no parent inside the trace. Materialised so the trace list never scans children.

fields.name: is_event
fields.doc: True for a point in time rather than a duration. Event spans have no end.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.doc: The kind of thing that produced this span.

fields.name: entity_id
fields.doc: Stable identifier of the producing entity.

fields.name: entity_name
fields.doc: Display name of the producing entity.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: What went in. For a model call this is the full prompt, and it is the single most valuable field mcpd stores.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: What came out. For a model call this is the completion.

fields.name: attributes
fields.doc: Kind-specific structured detail. See the attribute reference for what each kind carries.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Anything you want to attach. mcpd never interprets this.

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: Token counts, on model and embedding spans.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: Computed cost, on spans that consumed tokens.

fields.name: model_parameters
fields.doc: How the model was called: the sampling settings the caller chose. Absent on a span that made no model call, and on one whose producer did not record them.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Failure detail, when `status` is `error`.

fields.name: links
fields.doc: Causal references to other spans or traces.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Free labels for filtering. Only meaningful on a root span, where they label the whole trace.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Which project, environment, session, thread and user this belongs to.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: Model identifier, denormalised out of `attributes` so it can be indexed and grouped.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: Model provider, denormalised for the same reason.

fields.name: received_at
fields.doc: When mcpd accepted this span. Differs from `start_time` for buffered or replayed data, and is what retention is measured against.

fields.name: ingest_key
fields.doc: Producer-supplied idempotency key. A retried batch with the same key is accepted once.

indexes.doc: The trace list, newest first, scoped to a project.
Root-only projection for the trace list.
Cost and latency grouped by model.

Trace.doc: A whole run, projected from its spans. mcpd materialises this at ingest so the list view is one indexed read rather than an aggregation over every span. One per project and trace id: a trace id crosses service boundaries, so two projects that call each other each hold their own run under it, built from their own spans.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace this summarises.

fields.name: root_span_id
fields.doc: The root span, when one has arrived.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The root span's name.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: The root span's kind.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: `error` when any span in the trace failed, otherwise the root's status.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: Earliest start across the trace.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: Latest end across the trace. Absent while anything is still running.

fields.name: duration_ns
fields.doc: Wall-clock span of the whole trace.

fields.name: span_count
fields.doc: How many spans have arrived.

fields.name: error_count
fields.doc: How many of them failed.

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: Token usage summed across every model span in the trace.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: Cost summed across the trace. This is the number a bill is reconciled against.

fields.name: model_count
fields.doc: How many model calls the run made.

fields.name: tool_count
fields.doc: How many tool calls the run made.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Tags from the root span.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Context inherited from the root span.

fields.name: score_summary
fields.doc: Mean score per scorer id, maintained as scores arrive, so the list can sort by quality without a join.

fields.name: feedback_summary
fields.doc: Counts per feedback kind and value.

fields.name: is_complete
fields.doc: True once the root span has ended and no span is still open.

fields.name: received_at
fields.doc: When the first span of this trace arrived.

LogRecord.doc: A structured log line, correlated to the span that produced it. Logs are stored beside traces so 'show me the logs for this run' is one query, not a context switch to another tool.

fields.name: log_id
fields.doc: Unique id for this record.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace this line belongs to, when it was emitted inside one.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The span this line belongs to.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: When the line was emitted.

fields.name: level
fields.doc: Severity.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The rendered message.

fields.name: fields
fields.doc: Structured key/value context. Redacted like any payload.

fields.name: logger
fields.doc: Which logger emitted it.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Project, environment, session and user.

fields.name: received_at
fields.doc: When mcpd accepted it.

indexes.doc: All logs for a run, in order.

MetricPoint.doc: One numeric observation. mcpd aggregates these into time buckets on read, and keeps raw points only as long as the raw retention class allows.

fields.name: metric_id
fields.doc: Unique id for this observation.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Metric name, such as `mcpd.model.duration`.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: How it aggregates.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The observed value.

fields.name: unit
fields.doc: UCUM unit, such as `ms`, `By` or `{token}`.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: When it was observed.

fields.name: labels
fields.doc: Dimensions. Passed through the cardinality filter, which rejects unbounded keys.

fields.name: buckets
fields.doc: Histogram bucket boundaries and counts, on histogram points.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: Exemplar link: the trace that produced this observation.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: Exemplar link: the span that produced it. This is what turns a spike on a chart into a specific run you can open.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Project and environment.

fields.name: received_at
fields.doc: When mcpd accepted it.

Score.doc: A machine evaluation of a span or a trace.

fields.name: score_id
fields.doc: Unique id.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The scored trace.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The scored span, when the score is about one step rather than the whole run.

fields.name: scorer_id
fields.doc: Which scorer produced this, such as `answer_relevance`.

fields.name: scorer_version
fields.doc: The scorer's version. A score is only comparable to another score from the same version.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Live, offline, experiment or manual.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The numeric result.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: Lower bound of the scale. Without it, a bare number is not interpretable.

fields.name: max
fields.doc: Upper bound of the scale.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: A categorical result, when the scorer produces one alongside the number.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why. For an LLM judge this is the judge's explanation, and it is what makes a score arguable rather than magic.

fields.name: score_trace_id
fields.doc: The trace of the scoring run itself, so a suspicious score can be debugged like any other run.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: What producing this score cost. Judged evaluation is not free and mcpd refuses to hide that.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Anything else.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: When the score was produced.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Inherited from the target.

Feedback.doc: A human evaluation. Kept distinct from `Score` because the two answer different questions and must never be averaged together.

fields.name: feedback_id
fields.doc: Unique id.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace being judged.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The span being judged.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Thumbs, rating, correction, tag or comment.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The judgement. Its shape follows `kind`.

fields.name: comment
fields.doc: Free prose the person added.

fields.name: author_id
fields.doc: Who gave it. Hashed by default.

fields.name: author_kind
fields.doc: Whether the author was an end user, a reviewer or an operator.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: When it was given.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Anything else.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Inherited from the target.

Project.doc: The tenancy boundary. Every signal belongs to exactly one project; retention, redaction, sampling, budgets and access are all configured per project.

fields.name: project_id
fields.doc: Stable identifier, used in API paths and ingest keys.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.doc: How long to keep signals. Absent means the server default.

fields.name: sampling
fields.doc: The sampling policy for this project.

fields.name: redaction
fields.doc: Extra redaction rules, applied on top of the server defaults.

fields.name: budget
fields.doc: Cost budget and what happens when it is exceeded.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Anything else.

Dataset.doc: A fixed collection of inputs, with optional expected outputs, that an experiment runs against. Datasets are how a change is proved not to regress.

fields.name: dataset_id
fields.doc: Stable identifier.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: What this dataset is for.

fields.name: item_count
fields.doc: How many items it holds.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it was created.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Which project owns it.

fields.name: item_id
fields.doc: Stable identifier.

fields.name: dataset_id
fields.doc: Which dataset this belongs to.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: What to feed the system under test.

fields.name: expected
fields.doc: The reference answer, when there is one. Absent for open-ended cases judged by a scorer.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: Anything else, such as a difficulty label or a source citation.

fields.name: source_trace_id
fields.doc: The production trace this case was captured from, when it was. This is how a bug report becomes a permanent regression test.

Experiment.doc: One evaluation run of a system against a dataset. Comparing two experiments is how a change is accepted or rejected.

fields.name: experiment_id
fields.doc: Stable identifier.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name.

fields.name: dataset_id
fields.doc: What it ran against.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where it got to.

fields.name: started_at
fields.doc: When it began.

fields.name: finished_at
fields.doc: When it ended.

fields.name: item_count
fields.doc: Cases attempted.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc: Aggregate score per scorer, with mean, standard deviation and count.

fields.name: baseline_id
fields.doc: The experiment this one is compared against.

fields.name: cost
fields.doc: What the whole run cost.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed, when it did.

fields.name: metadata
fields.doc: The configuration under test: model, prompt version, git sha.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Which project owns it.

AuditEvent.doc: One recorded attempt to read stored payloads, or to delete them. Written by the handlers that hand prompts and completions back out of mcpd, so the question "who read this run" has an answer. The audit log is not trimmed by the retention pass: a log that deleted itself on the same schedule as the data it describes could not say who read the data that has since gone.

fields.name: audit_id
fields.doc: Unique id.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: When the request was handled.

fields.name: principal
fields.doc: Which key acted, as a short hex digest of it. The key itself is never written here. `anonymous` when the request carried no key, which is what an unprotected daemon looks like.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: The end identity a proxy asserted for this request. Always empty in this build. The field exists from the first release so that proxy identity can be added later without a migration.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: What was done, named as the endpoint id: `get_trace`, `list_spans`, `delete_trace`.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: The project the request was made against.

fields.name: resource
fields.doc: The trace or dataset the request named, when it named one.

fields.name: result
fields.doc: Whether authorisation allowed the request or refused it.

indexes.doc: One project's audit log, newest first.

Definition.doc: A stored definition. Immutable per version: a run pins the version it started against, and that version never changes underneath it.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project owns it.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Its identifier within the project.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: Its version. A run started without one pins the highest stored version at that moment.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What kind of definition it is.

fields.name: body
fields.doc: The document as stored, minus `version`.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When this version was stored.

Run.doc: One execution of one definition version. The daemon owns the run between steps: its journal, its deadlines, its waits, its cancel and its trace. Your own process owns everything inside a step.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Its identifier, minted at start.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project owns it.

fields.name: definition_id
fields.doc: Which definition it runs.

fields.name: definition_version
fields.doc: Which version. Pinned at start and never re-resolved.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where it is.

fields.name: cursor
fields.doc: The frontier: where in the graph the run has reached.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: What it was started with, after validation against the definition's `input_schema`.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: What the definition's `output` template rendered when the run reached the end of the graph.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: A JSON object merged shallowly on every `complete` that sends one. Later steps read it through the lease.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed, when it did: the failing step's message, or the ceiling it spent.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: The context stored at start and copied onto every span the daemon writes for the run, with `run_id` set to this run's id.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace every span of this run belongs to. 32 lowercase hex characters, minted at start.

fields.name: steps_used
fields.doc: How many steps this run has completed. Counted against `max_steps` on the root of the run tree.

fields.name: max_steps
fields.doc: The step ceiling from the definition's `limits`, when it declares one. On a root it bounds the whole tree.

fields.name: cost_usd
fields.doc: What the run's steps have cost so far, priced from the usage workers reported.

fields.name: max_cost_usd
fields.doc: The spend ceiling from `limits`, when declared. A claim refused for a spent ceiling ends the run `failed`.

fields.name: deadline_at
fields.doc: When `limits.run_timeout_ms` passes. Absent when the definition declares no timeout, and once the run has ended.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc: The key the start request carried, when it carried one. A repost of it within 24 hours returns this run.

fields.name: root_run_id
fields.doc: The root of the run tree, which ceilings are enforced against. Equal to `run_id` on a root.

fields.name: parent_run_id
fields.doc: The run whose `subworkflow` step started this one.

fields.name: parent_step_key
fields.doc: The step in the parent that this run is the body of.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How many parents lie between this run and the root. Zero on a root.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When it started.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc: When it last moved.

fields.name: ended_at
fields.doc: When it reached a terminal status.

StepAttempt.doc: One attempt at one step of a run. A run's journal is these rows, append only: a retry is a new row, never a rewrite of the old one.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Which run.

fields.name: step_key
fields.doc: Which step, with any enclosing branch, item or iteration folded into the key: `refund/issue`, `classify[3]`, `poll[7]/classify`.

fields.name: attempt
fields.doc: Which attempt this is. The fence: a lease for an earlier attempt is refused once a later one exists.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What kind of step.

fields.name: effect
fields.doc: What a duplicated body would cost.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where the attempt is.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: The rendered input handed to the worker, on a claimable step.

fields.name: output
fields.doc: What the worker returned on `complete`, or the event payload on a resumed wait.

fields.name: error
fields.doc: Why it failed, when it did.

fields.name: usage
fields.doc: The token usage the worker reported on `complete`.

fields.name: cost_usd
fields.doc: What the daemon priced that usage at.

fields.name: span_id
fields.doc: The span the daemon opened for this attempt. 16 lowercase hex characters, minted when the row was written. A worker's own spans nest under it.

fields.name: lease_owner
fields.doc: The `worker_id` holding the lease, while one does.

fields.name: lease_until
fields.doc: When the lease lapses without a heartbeat.

fields.name: started_at
fields.doc: When the worker posted `started`. Absent when it never did, which is what the reclaim rule reads.

fields.name: orphaned_at
fields.doc: When the lease lapsed.

fields.name: reclaim_until
fields.doc: When the reclaim window closes.

fields.name: attempts_left
fields.doc: How many attempts the node's retry budget still allows after this one.

fields.name: ended_at
fields.doc: When it reached a terminal status.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the row was written.

RunEvent.doc: One row of a run's event log. Written in the transaction that made the change it describes, with `seq` allocated from the run header, so a reader that has seen a row has seen every row below it.

fields.name: run_id
fields.doc: Which run.

fields.name: seq
fields.doc: Its position in this run's stream, from zero and without gaps. Pass it as `after` to reattach.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What happened.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: The detail, shaped by `kind`.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: When it was written.

Aspect.doc: An axis that traces are described along. An aspect is a definition and not a measurement: it carries the name a note is filed under, the words an operator reads on screen and, where a model writes the sentence, the instruction handed to whatever produces it. Four ship with the daemon as ordinary rows rather than as a list compiled into a client, so there is one source of truth for what exists: goal, what the user wanted; sentiment, the tone they expressed; behaviour, what the agent did about it; and outcome, how the interaction ended. A stored version never changes, so a note recorded a month ago still names the definition it was written against.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project owns it. Aspects are project-scoped, like every other tenancy boundary here.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The aspect's name, lowercase with underscores, such as `goal` or `refund_reason`. This is what a note is filed under and what every query parameter names.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The display name, such as `Goal`. Stored rather than derived from the name, so an aspect reads the same in every screen and every language of SDK.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: One line saying what this axis is about, shown beside the label so a reader does not have to infer the axis from its name.

fields.name: instruction
fields.doc: The text handed to whatever writes a note along this aspect, at most 2000 bytes. The daemon stores it and hands it out; what reads it and writes the sentence sits outside the daemon. Absent when `derived` is true, because a derived aspect needs no instruction.

fields.name: derived
fields.doc: Whether the daemon writes this aspect's notes itself, with no model anywhere. `outcome` ships derived, written from the run's status, the step error class, the silent producer flag on the cause report and the divergence watch, so a deployment with nothing configured still fills one aspect and can see the whole pipeline work before a model is wired to anything.

fields.name: built_in
fields.doc: Whether the daemon seeded this aspect. A built-in is a row like any other and can be switched off, but it cannot be deleted, because notes already name it.

fields.name: enabled
fields.doc: Whether notes are written along this aspect in this project. It is configuration and read-only here. Switching an aspect on affects notes recorded afterwards and never rewrites what is stored.

fields.name: sort_order
fields.doc: Where this aspect sits in every list and in the default column order, ascending. Stored, so the order an operator learns is the order they keep.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: This definition's version. Editing an aspect stores a new version rather than changing this one, so analysis already recorded is never rewritten under a reader.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When this version was stored.

indexes.doc: The catalogue, in the order it is shown.

AspectNote.doc: One sentence recorded against one trace along one aspect. A note proves one thing: that this sentence was recorded against that trace by the definition named in `aspect`, at the version in `definition_version`. It does not prove the sentence is true. Nothing here is checked against the trace it describes, so a note is evidence of what a definition said and not evidence of what happened, and the trace is what settles the difference. The daemon also keeps a small sketch of the wording, which is what clustering compares, and that sketch is deliberately not a field on this entity: it is a detail of how the pass is stored, a caller can do nothing with it, and publishing it would fix the hashing where it stands today. The text is payload. It passes through the same redactor as every other signal on the way in, retention sweeps it, and erasing a subject erases it.

fields.name: note_id
fields.doc: Unique id of the note. This identifies the sentence and never the run: a note id and a trace id are different things and conflating them is the mistake this separate name exists to prevent.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.doc: The trace this sentence is about.

fields.name: aspect
fields.doc: Which aspect this note is filed under, matching `Aspect.name`.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: The sentence, after redaction. It is the only text the read API returns for a note, and it is what the clustering pass reads.

fields.name: definition_version
fields.doc: The version of the aspect definition this note was written against. Editing a definition mints a new version, so an older note keeps naming what was actually asked for at the time.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: Which model wrote the sentence, when one did. Absent for a derived aspect, where the daemon wrote the note itself.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the note was recorded. Writing a note lags the trace it describes, sometimes by a long way, so a trace can be visible for hours before it carries one.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc: Inherited from the trace, so a note is scoped, filtered, retained and erased exactly as its trace is.

indexes.doc: One aspect's notes newest first, which is the order a clustering pass reads them in.

ThemeSnapshot.doc: One clustering pass over one entity, covering a moving window of notes. A snapshot is what turns a clustering into a series: every theme belongs to exactly one, and every theme query names one. Windows overlap, so counts from two snapshots must never be added together. A trace whose note falls inside three windows is counted once in each of them, and summing the three counts it three times. Compare snapshots or read one; do not sum them. Reads never recompute either: a pass writes a snapshot on its own timer and every read is a lookup of what it wrote, so refreshing a screen shows the same numbers rather than a fresh clustering.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.doc: Opaque id, echoed back unchanged. Never build one by hand and never read meaning into its shape.

fields.name: project
fields.doc: Which project this pass covered.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.doc: The kind of thing this pass covered.

fields.name: entity_name
fields.doc: The name of that thing. An entity is the pair of a kind and a name, which spans already carry, so nothing new is assigned to identify one.

fields.name: aspects
fields.doc: The aspects this pass covered, in catalogue order. An aspect with too few notes when the pass ran is absent, so a missing name means it is still collecting and not that anything failed.

fields.name: ordinal
fields.doc: Where this snapshot falls in the entity's series, counting from one at the oldest snapshot still stored.

fields.name: cutoff_at
fields.doc: When this snapshot became the current state. A timeline is ordered by this and not by the window bounds, because two passes can cover overlapping windows.

fields.name: window_from
fields.doc: Start of the window of notes read, inclusive.

fields.name: window_to
fields.doc: End of the window of notes read, exclusive.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many distinct traces the notes read belong to.

fields.name: note_count
fields.doc: How many notes the pass actually read. Every coverage figure in this snapshot is a share of this number and never of the number of notes in the window, which is what makes `capped` worth reading.

fields.name: capped
fields.doc: Whether the pass reached its ceiling of 20,000 notes and clustered the newest of them rather than all of them. True means the window holds more notes than were read, so the denominator of every share here is `note_count` and not the window.

indexes.doc: One entity's series of passes, newest first.

Theme.doc: A cluster of aspect notes that share their wording, in one snapshot along one aspect. A theme groups aspect notes that share their wording, which is why mcpd needs no model and no embedding to build one. It does not read the sentences, so two notes that mean the same thing in different words land in separate themes, and a theme's label is the note most like the others rather than a summary written for it. The clustering is a pure function of the notes it reads, with no floating-point arithmetic in the comparison, so two replicas of one deployment reading the same notes write the same themes and cannot disagree about where a boundary falls.

fields.name: theme_id
fields.doc: Opaque id, stable across snapshots, which is what makes a history possible. A theme keeps its id while its wording holds, so the same id in two snapshots is the same theme. Nothing is encoded in the shape of it.

fields.name: snapshot_id
fields.doc: The snapshot this theme belongs to.

fields.name: aspect
fields.doc: Which aspect it was clustered along. Clustering runs once per aspect, so one trace can sit in a different theme in each of them.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.doc: The kind of entity this theme was built for.

fields.name: entity_name
fields.doc: The name of that entity.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The theme's label, which is the text of one of its own notes: the note most like the rest of them. Nothing wrote it for the screen, so it reads as one real sentence about one real trace rather than as a description of the group, and it can change between snapshots as the group does.

fields.name: label_note_id
fields.doc: The note the label is taken from.

fields.name: label_trace_id
fields.doc: The trace that note was written about, so a reader can open the run behind the label instead of taking the label's word for it.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: What happened to this theme between the previous snapshot and this one.

fields.name: note_count
fields.doc: How many notes are in this theme.

fields.name: trace_count
fields.doc: How many distinct traces those notes were written about.

fields.name: coverage
fields.doc: This theme's share of the notes the snapshot read for this aspect, between 0 and 1. The denominator is the snapshot's `note_count`, so in a capped snapshot it is a share of what was read.

indexes.doc: One theme across every snapshot that holds it, which is what a history reads.

endpoints.doc: The standard OTLP/HTTP trace endpoint. Accepts protobuf (`application/x-protobuf`) and JSON (`application/json`), gzip-encoded or uncompressed, and answers in the encoding it was sent. Point any OpenTelemetry SDK here and mcpd will record its spans, mapping GenAI and OpenInference semantic conventions onto mcpd's own model. Span links and span events are kept. This is the endpoint that makes mcpd framework-agnostic: nothing about it requires an mcpd SDK. The same port also serves OTLP over gRPC.

The standard OTLP/HTTP log endpoint. Accepts protobuf (`application/x-protobuf`) and JSON (`application/json`), gzip-encoded or uncompressed, and answers in the encoding it was sent. Records correlate to spans automatically through their trace and span ids, and a resent export is recognised and stored once.

The standard OTLP/HTTP metric endpoint. Accepts protobuf (`application/x-protobuf`) and JSON (`application/json`), gzip-encoded or uncompressed, and answers in the encoding it was sent. Exemplars are kept, and mcpd turns them into links back to the exact span that produced a data point. A resent export is recognised and stored once.

Accepts mcpd's own shapes for all five signals in one batch, posted as a single `IngestBatch` object, gzip-encoded or uncompressed. Use this when you want the full model without translating through OTLP: token detail, cost, scores and feedback all survive intact. Supply `ingest_key` on a batch to make retries idempotent.

The OTLP/gRPC trace service, on the same port as everything else. The listener takes cleartext HTTP/2 beside HTTP/1.1, so an exporter set to `grpc` needs only this daemon's address. Send the key as `authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata. Messages may be gzip-compressed. Every span takes the same road as one sent to `POST /v1/traces`.

The OTLP/gRPC logs service, on the same port as everything else. Send the key as `authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata. Messages may be gzip-compressed. Every record takes the same road as one sent to `POST /v1/logs`.

The OTLP/gRPC metrics service, on the same port as everything else. Send the key as `authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata. Messages may be gzip-compressed. Every data point takes the same road as one sent to `POST /v1/metrics`.

The Zipkin v2 span endpoint. Accepts a JSON array of spans (`application/json`) or a proto3 `ListOfSpans` (`application/x-protobuf`), gzip-encoded or uncompressed, so a Zipkin reporter needs only this daemon's address. `localEndpoint.serviceName` becomes the service, tags become attributes, `kind` becomes the `span.kind` attribute, annotations become span events, and the `error` tag sets the status. A shared server span is stored under an id derived from the one it shares, parented to it, so both halves are kept. Answers `202` with the counts.

The Jaeger collector's HTTP endpoint. Takes one `jaeger.Batch` in Thrift's binary protocol (`application/x-thrift`), gzip-encoded or uncompressed. The process becomes the service and its tags the resource, span tags become attributes, logs become span events, and references become the parent and span links: the first `CHILD_OF` in the same trace is the parent, and every other reference is a link whose kind is `child_of` or `follows_from`. Answers `202` with the counts.

The Jaeger collector's gRPC service, on the same port as everything else. Send the key as `authorization: Bearer <key>` metadata. Messages may be gzip-compressed. Spans are mapped exactly as `POST /api/traces` maps them.

The trace list. Filter on status, kind, name, tags, session, thread, user, environment, model, time window, duration, cost and score, and sort by start time, duration, cost, span count or score. Unlike a plain span dump, this reads the materialised trace projection rather than aggregating spans on every request.

query.name: q
query.doc: Full-text search across span names, prompts and completions. This is the field that answers 'find the run where the model said that'.

query.name: kind
query.doc: Only traces whose root is this kind.

query.name: tags
query.doc: Traces carrying all of these tags.

query.name: user_id
query.doc: Every trace for one end user. Stored ids are hashed, and this value is hashed the same way before matching, so pass the plain id you sent.

query.name: from
query.doc: Start of the time window, inclusive.

query.name: to
query.doc: End of the time window, exclusive.

query.name: min_duration_ms
query.doc: Only traces at least this slow.

query.name: min_cost
query.doc: Only traces at least this expensive.

query.name: has_score
query.doc: Only traces carrying a score from this scorer.

query.name: score_below
query.doc: Combined with `has_score`: only traces where that scorer came in under this value. This is the query that finds bad answers.

query.name: cursor
query.doc: Opaque cursor from a previous page.

endpoints.summary: Get one trace with every span
endpoints.doc: Returns the trace projection and the full span tree in one response, ordered so a client can render the waterfall without a second request or a client-side sort.

query.name: include
query.doc: Comma-separated extras: `logs`, `scores`, `feedback`, `metrics`. Fetching a run and everything attached to it is one request.

endpoints.summary: Delete a trace and everything attached to it
endpoints.doc: Removes the trace, its spans, logs, metrics, scores and feedback. Used to satisfy an erasure request. The deletion is recorded in the audit log.

endpoints.summary: List the projects that have data
endpoints.doc: Every project mcpd has stored a signal for. Projects are not created up front: a project exists as soon as something arrives carrying its name, which is why this reads the data rather than a registry.

endpoints.summary: The values a filter dimension takes
endpoints.doc: What to offer in a filter box. A filter is only usable if you know what to type into it, and the values are not a fixed list: they are whatever the services reporting to this project happen to send. This reads the distinct-value list the daemon maintains as signals arrive, scoped to one project, prefix-matched for typeahead and ordered by value. Ask for one dimension at a time. One limit is worth knowing before you build against it: `metric_label_key` lists every label key seen anywhere in the project, not the keys of one named metric, because the list is keyed by the label and not by the metric that carried it.

query.name: project
query.doc: Which project to read. Every dimension is scoped to one.

query.name: key
query.doc: For `metric_label_value`, the label key whose values you want. Required for that facet, because the answer would otherwise be every label's values mixed together. Ignored by every other facet.

query.name: prefix
query.doc: Offer only values starting with this. Matched literally and case sensitively, because these values are what a filter will be compared against and folding here would offer one that then matches nothing.

query.name: limit
query.doc: How many values to return, up to 1000. A filter box shows a list somebody reads; ten thousand environments is not a longer list, it is a slower request that renders the same first page.

The body names the capability in its `capability` field, using the same word `GET /v1/api/capabilities` publishes, so a caller can read the capability set once and stop asking rather than retrying a refusal that will never change.

endpoints.summary: What has arrived since you last looked
endpoints.doc: Refresh a list in place instead of running its query again. Hold the cursor from the last poll, send it back, and get the rows that have arrived since, oldest first. The watermark is a row's arrival time and its id together, because a batch writes every row in it with one timestamp and a watermark that could only say 'after this nanosecond' would either replay the whole batch or skip the rest of it. A row written with an arrival time behind the watermark, which a sender can cause by setting `received_at` itself, is not returned; that is the cost of a watermark and no cursor shape avoids it.

query.name: signal
query.doc: Which signal to poll. Defaults to `traces`.

query.name: cursor
query.doc: The cursor the previous poll returned, unchanged. Absent starts from `since`, or from the oldest row the project holds when that is absent too. A cursor this daemon did not issue is refused rather than guessed at.

query.name: since
query.doc: Where to start when there is no cursor yet. Ignored once `cursor` is set.
